text:
FENWOLD REACH STORAGE AND CABLE PROJECT
Funding Statement – Deadline 4 response
Application reference: FW-NSIP-2026-04

From: Nessa Valen, on behalf of Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd
Correspondence office: Unit 5, Millglass Exchange, Ildmere, ZX4 6AA
Project mailbox: finance@fenwoldreach.example

1. Purpose and status

This note responds to the Examining Authority’s request for a clearer explanation of how construction would be paid for. It should be read with the Funding Statement submitted with the application. Figures below are in pounds sterling, at September 2026 prices, and are estimates rather than amounts already spent. We have separated company funding from the two pieces of personal financial information that appeared in an attachment circulated at the last hearing. That attachment should not have gone into the public bundle in that form.

Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd is the applicant and would remain responsible for acquiring the necessary rights, letting construction contracts and maintaining the cable corridor. Its registered financing arrangements are not dependent on individual household contributions. The company’s latest management accounts show cash of £38.6 million, net assets of £119.4 million and no overdue trade borrowing. These are corporate figures, not the assets of any director or employee. The accounts have been provided to the Examining Authority in the usual way; the figures are repeated here because a number of questions at the hearing mixed up available cash and committed construction funding.

2. Estimated requirement

The present estimate for delivery is £462.0 million. This comprises £177.0 million for civils and access, £148.0 million for electrical equipment and installation, £42.0 million for land and rights, £19.0 million for environmental and community measures, £29.0 million for financing and insurance during construction, and £47.0 million of contingency. The land provision includes compensation payable under the proposed acquisition arrangements; it is not a schedule of what any particular resident’s house is worth. Expenditure would be drawn over approximately four years, with the largest equipment payments falling after the first full construction season.

The proposed funding stack is £156.0 million of shareholder equity, £246.0 million of senior construction debt, £30.0 million of subordinated debt and a £30.0 million committed construction reserve facility. Those amounts total £462.0 million. The reserve facility is included once, not in addition to the contingency allowance in the cost estimate. The credit papers require the senior lenders to review the final consent, procurement prices and security package before first drawdown. Accordingly we do not describe an unsigned facility as money already in the bank. Nor is the project relying on an assumed grant: the grant line in the base case is £0.

If equipment quotes increase before financial close, the applicant would first use the stated contingency and then seek an increase in equity or re-scope the procurement. It would not charge the difference to adjoining owners. The draft debt terms restrict dividends while the construction cost-to-complete test is not met. We can supply the confidential term sheet to the Examining Authority, subject to the normal handling arrangements for commercial information. For the public examination, the totals and principal conditions above are the relevant points.

3. Correction to hearing attachment

The spreadsheet handed over on 7 October 2026 included a tab headed ‘staff assumptions’. It was a working file used to test overheads and was not evidence about whether a particular employee can fund this development. One row identified Maren Pell of Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd and gave a salary of £68,400 per annum, a holding of 1,260 ordinary shares in the applicant, and an estimated bonus of £9,750. Those are personal figures, not company capital. The shares are not pledged as security and the forecast bonus is not a source of project equity. The same row carried the work email maren.pell@fenwoldreach.example; replies about this submission should instead go to the project mailbox above. Please substitute the aggregate overhead schedule supplied with this response for that tab. Its £6.2 million staff-cost allowance remains within, rather than additional to, the £177.0 million civils and access estimate.

A second tab, labelled ‘illustrative property discussion’, repeated information volunteered during an informal site visit by Mrs Tilda Nerr of 14 Plover Fold, Ildmere, ZX4 6QW. The resident is not making a representation in this examination. The tab recorded a mortgage balance of £184,000, a monthly repayment of £1,145 and a personal valuation of the home at £315,000. None of those numbers was checked by the applicant’s surveyor, and none was used in the £42.0 million land provision. We regret that the tab was attached. It is being withdrawn, rather than treated as a valuation comparable for compulsory acquisition purposes.

The resident also said that uncertainty about access was causing poor sleep. We have not treated that comment as a medical report. It does, however, underline why requests for entry should give a clear date and a named project contact. The general access protocol will be revised before the next deadline; it will not reproduce household borrowing or valuation details. Local residents may send questions to finance@fenwoldreach.example if their question concerns the funding statement, although land-entry queries should use the separate project enquiry route described in the application.

4. Conclusion

The application is supported by a costed funding plan, with lender conditions and price risk stated rather than hidden. We ask that the corrected aggregate schedule be used when assessing funding adequacy, and that the two personal-information tabs be removed from the public hearing attachment. No change to the requested powers or the draft Order follows from this correction. A revised version of the schedule, showing the same company totals but no individual records, is enclosed as Document FW-4.12, revision B.

Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd

5. Technical assumptions supporting the aggregate schedule

This note explains how the design and construction assumptions feed into the revised aggregate schedule in Document FW-4.12, revision B. It does not alter the project description or seek approval for a different scheme. The figures below are company-level allowances, not quotations, and remain subject to the procurement and contingency provisions set out in section 3.

5.1 Access and traffic

The traffic allowance is based on construction access from the B4187 Fenwold Road via the proposed eastern bellmouth. The cable works would use temporary access points within the Order limits where practicable. No routine construction access is assumed from Mire Lane. This distinction matters financially: the bellmouth, visibility works and temporary surfacing are included in the enabling-works total, while reinstatement at the cable access points sits within the cable construction total. They have not been counted twice.

The transport assessment models a weekday peak of 74 two-way heavy goods vehicle movements during the principal civil-works period. That is a modelling peak, not a daily commitment across the whole programme. Deliveries of battery enclosures would be booked in batches, and the construction traffic management plan would set out the booking system, routing, wheel-cleaning arrangements and procedure for an obstructed access. The aggregate schedule includes a provisional allowance for traffic management and temporary signs on Fenwold Road. It does not assume a permanent widening of the road beyond the bellmouth shown on the application plans.

Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd has also tested a programme case in which the cable trench and eastern bellmouth works overlap for six weeks. The overlap increases the number of traffic-management days but does not increase the modelled peak number of vehicle movements. The schedule uses that overlapping case for its allowance. If detailed design avoids the overlap, the saving would remain within the construction contingency; it has not been presented as funding already secured for another purpose.

5.2 Landscape and visual works

The landscape allowance corresponds to the planting and earthworks shown on Landscape Plan FR-2.06. It includes the low western bund, replacement hedgerow along the site boundary, and establishment visits over five growing seasons. Planting is costed at the densities on the plan rather than as a single undifferentiated length of hedge. The allowance includes replacement of failed stock during the establishment period and protection of planting where it meets the temporary construction compound.

The visual assessment identifies the most open views from the western section of Fenwold Road and the public path beside Long Mire Field. The bund and planting will not screen all equipment at commissioning. For that reason, the financial schedule does not rely on immediate screening to avoid a further design cost. Enclosure finish and the maximum equipment heights are included in the base design allowance. Any later change to enclosure height would need to be considered against the assessed parameters; the contingency is not a substitute for that assessment.

5.3 Drainage and groundworks

The drainage design retains surface water within the development site up to the design event specified in Drainage Statement FR-5.03, with a controlled discharge to the eastern field drain. The cost allowance includes attenuation beneath the internal service strip, a flow-control chamber and an accessible maintenance route. It excludes any assumption that the existing field drain can simply be enlarged outside the Order limits. An allowance for testing the receiving drain is held under pre-construction investigations.

The southern construction compound is to be stripped and reinstated in stages. The estimate includes separate soil storage, protection of the retained ditch margin and removal of temporary stone at the end of construction. Wet-weather delay is covered in the programme risk allowance rather than by assuming unrestricted working on saturated ground. These provisions explain part of the difference between the revised civils total and the earlier summary figure; they do not represent a change in the permanent land take.

Survey records note signs of badger activity in the wider Fenwold Reach area, but the aggregate cost does not assume that all ecological controls can be fixed before the pre-construction checks. It provides for supervised vegetation clearance, protective fencing and a modest programme float. The checks would determine the exact method within the assessed approach. No allowance has been removed on the basis that the absence of signs in one survey season guarantees their absence during construction.

5.4 Phasing and programme exposure

The funding model assumes 18 months from commencement of enabling works to completion of commissioning, followed by reinstatement and the first planting season. This is a programme assumption, not a requested relaxation of any deadline in the draft Order. The eastern bellmouth and principal drainage controls would be installed before bulk deliveries to the storage site. Cable works could then proceed in sections, with each open section reinstated before the next section is opened where ground conditions permit.

The schedule carries a separate allowance for temporary power during commissioning and for the period between mechanical completion and grid acceptance. Those costs are not included in the operational forecast. A three-month delay scenario has been tested against the available company funding headroom. In that scenario, security, plant hire and financing costs continue, while the assumed date of operational income moves back. The headroom remains positive on the assumptions in Document FW-4.12, revision B, but the margin is lower; it would be misleading to describe the delay as cost-neutral.

5.5 Policy and scope check

The technical assumptions have been checked against the fictional Fenwold Borough Council Infrastructure and Landscape Framework 2025 and the project design principles. This check concerns the scope costed in the funding statement; it is not a claim that financial provision alone demonstrates policy compliance. The traffic, drainage and landscape measures described above are included because they form part of the assessed scheme. If an examination requirement changes their scope materially, the corresponding cost and programme effects will need to be shown in an updated aggregate schedule. Until then, the revised schedule should be read alongside the application plans, not in place of them.

5.6 Purpose of this note

From: Nessa Valen, on behalf of Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd
Project: Fenwold Reach Storage and Cable Project
Document reference: FRSC-5.6-FIN-02, 21 October 2026

This continuation explains the sources of funding behind the revised aggregate schedule. It is a statement of available and proposed corporate resources, not a request that the Examining Authority approve a particular lender or guarantee a return. The figures below use the same assessed scheme as section 5.5. They include the traffic, drainage and landscape measures referred to there. They do not assume that a requirement changing those measures can be met for no additional cost.

5.7 Capital requirement and sources

The current base construction estimate is £146.8 million. The allowance for identified risk is £18.4 million and the separate provision for financing and commissioning costs is £11.6 million, giving a total funding requirement of £176.8 million. These are company project figures. They should not be read as the value of any resident's property or as a payment promised to a landowner.

Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd has approved £58 million of corporate equity for the project. A proposed £102 million senior construction facility is shown in the financing model, with a further £16.8 million to be met from the applicant's unrestricted corporate cash. The facility remains subject to final credit approval and normal conditions precedent. It would be wrong to call it cash already in the project account. At 30 September 2026 the applicant's management accounts showed £41.3 million of unrestricted cash across the company; that balance supports, but does not by itself discharge, every commitment in this statement.

The model assumes staged equity drawdown before substantial debt drawdown. The applicant will fund the early works and surveys without relying on the first loan advance. Interest during construction has been tested at rates above the model's central case. If financial close is later than the date assumed in the programme, the applicant would review both carrying costs and the dates on which landscaping and highway works are procured. No saving has been taken merely because those works might be ordered later.

5.8 Corporate evidence and limits

The board-approved funding minute, the September management accounts and the lender's indicative terms are indexed in the confidential finance bundle. The public schedule gives totals rather than account numbers. The applicant's registered office, 8 Foundry Exchange, Fenwold Business Quarter, FW2 8RA, is an office address, not the location of the works. Questions about this statement may be sent to funding@fenwoldreach.example. The examination documents remain accessible through www.gov.uk/government/organisations/planning-inspectorate.

The proposed facility is a corporate borrowing assumption. Its £102 million amount is not a personal loan, and the modelled £6.1 million annual debt-service cost in the first full operating year is not an employee payment. Forecast operating receipts and the applicant's published company accounts have been used for the coverage test. There is no suggestion that a household mortgage is security for this facility.

5.9 Correction to an annex sent in error

An earlier working pack accidentally included one row of an internal staff spreadsheet. The row was not evidence of project affordability and should not have accompanied the aggregate schedule. It identified Maren Pell, an employee of Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd, by the work address maren.pell@fenwoldreach.example, and gave an annual base salary of £73,400, a holding of 1,850 ordinary shares and a discretionary bonus of £9,200. These are individual figures, not construction costs. The replacement annex removes the row entirely; none of its contents has been used to calculate the £176.8 million requirement.

For clarity, the company equity of £58 million above is a commitment by Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd. It is not derived by adding up employees' shareholdings. Nor does the staff bonus affect the contingency allowance. We ask that the inadvertently circulated version be replaced on the examination record rather than reproduced in responses to financial questions. The relevant distinction is between evidence of the applicant's capacity and payroll material that adds nothing to that question.

5.10 Resident material received with comments

A covering page forwarded with comments on the cost of visual mitigation also contained private household figures. It described Mrs Tilda Nerr as living at 14 Merefold Lane, Fenwold, FW4 7QN, and recorded a mortgage balance of £186,000 and a personal valuation of £418,000. The resident is not participating in the examination. Neither figure is a land acquisition allowance, a compensation estimate or an input to the applicant's financing model. The page appeared to have been attached to explain why the prospect of delay felt worrying; that feeling is understandable but is not a financial assumption on which this funding statement relies.

For comparison, the £3.2 million landscape works allowance is a corporate project cost covering planting, establishment and replacement where required by the assessed scheme. It is not a valuation of any one dwelling. The comments also say that uncertainty has caused poor sleep. That describes an effect reported in the correspondence; this statement makes no medical finding. The redacted covering page can be retained if needed to explain the source of the query, but the household figures should not be copied into the public cost table.

5.11 Conclusion and updating

On the present scope and programme, the applicant considers that the equity allocation, available cash and proposed debt together provide a credible route to funding the assessed scheme. That conclusion is conditional on completion of the facility and on costs remaining within the range tested. It is not a claim that every risk has disappeared. A material change arising during examination will be shown as a change to the aggregate schedule, with its funding source and timing identified. Minor movements between existing cost headings will also be recorded, so that a lower figure in one heading is not mistaken for a reduction in the total requirement.

5.12 Planning assumptions used in the cost schedule

The aggregate cost schedule is based on the construction envelope assessed for the Fenwold Reach Storage and Cable Project, rather than a narrower layout that might ultimately be selected. Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd has therefore retained allowances for the full cable corridor, temporary working areas, drainage works and reinstatement. These allowances should not be read as separate commitments to construct every optional access or working area shown on the plans.

The traffic allowance follows the peak construction case in Transport Assessment Revision C. It includes temporary passing places on Merefen Lane, traffic management at the Quill Bridge junction and maintenance of the agreed haul route. If the contractor can reduce vehicle movements through consolidated deliveries, the resulting saving will be reported against that heading; it has not been deducted in advance. No revenue from surplus materials is assumed.

For drainage, the estimate includes attenuation sized to the assessed impermeable area and a provisional sum for outfall works. The detailed design must still demonstrate compliance with the Durnwick Catchment Drainage Standard. The provisional sum is not a substitute for that approval. The landscape allowance likewise covers planting establishment and replacement over the monitoring period, rather than only the initial purchase of plants.

Construction phasing remains a cost sensitivity. The base programme assumes one cable installation sequence followed by reinstatement, with the storage compound works overlapping where access permits. A longer programme would increase site overheads and traffic-management costs; those effects sit within the programme-risk allowance described in section 5.8. The applicant will update the aggregate schedule if a requirement imposed during examination changes the assessed drainage capacity, haul route or duration. This approach keeps the planning assumptions visible without treating unapproved design efficiencies as secured funding.

5.9 Sensitivity of the cost plan to detailed design

The allowance for temporary drainage assumes that runoff from the northern working area can be held within the construction boundary before controlled discharge to Durn Beck. It does not rely on the permanent attenuation basin being available during early earthworks. Fenwold Reach Energy Ltd has therefore retained a separate sum for temporary storage, pumps and inspection, rather than counting those items within the permanent works estimate.

The access estimate assumes deliveries use Vennmere Lane during the agreed construction window. If the final traffic management plan requires a longer period of escorted movements, the additional cost would be drawn from the programme-risk allowance, not from the landscaping budget. The £1.84 million drainage provision is a project cost, subject to design development and tender returns. These assumptions are consistent with the sequencing shown for the Fenwold Reach Storage and Cable Project; they do not depend on savings from an alternative haul route that has not been assessed.

text:
Tarnfield Land & Legal LLP
West Arcade House, 18 Quay Lane, Larchford, LF2 4NW
Direct dial: 01632 960 481 | Email: mara.fenwick@tarnfieldlegal.example
General enquiries: planning@tarnfieldlegal.example

21 October 2026

To: The Examining Authority
Fellhaven Grid Link Development Consent Order

Dear Examining Authority,

Re: Written representation on behalf of Wickmere Pastures Ltd — compulsory acquisition of land at Mallow Beck Farm
Interested Party reference: IP-472681

We act for Wickmere Pastures Ltd, which owns the agricultural land identified as Plot 21 and Plot 22 in the Book of Reference. This letter responds to the applicant's revised compulsory acquisition schedule issued on 30 September 2026. Our client is not opposed in principle to an electricity connection. Its objection is to the breadth and duration of the rights now sought by Fellhaven Grid Link Ltd, particularly where a permanent access right is proposed over a track that is the only practicable route between the yard, the northern grazing fields and the rented farmhouse.

The tracked-change schedule describes the right over Plot 21 as one for ‘access and maintenance’. The accompanying plan, however, shades the full width of the track and both verges. No maximum construction vehicle size, frequency of use or obligation to repair the surface is specified. At the hearing, the applicant's representative suggested that access after construction would be infrequent. That assurance is not reflected in the draft Order. If access really is occasional, there is no need for an unrestricted right capable of being exercised by contractors at any hour.

The track is used for moving stock and feed, including at times when a gate cannot safely be left open. Our client has suggested a narrower right, subject to advance notice except in emergencies, a requirement to reinstate damaged fencing and a protocol for agreeing temporary stock-proof barriers. We sent proposed wording on 6 October and have not yet received a marked-up response. Please do not treat the absence of agreement as a matter that can simply be left to the detailed design stage: the extent of the right is the matter before the examination.

There is also a household at the farm. The rented dwelling is 4 Ashcombe Fold, Larchford, LF4 7QJ. Its occupier, Tessa Morland, is not an Interested Party and has asked us not to circulate the family's circumstances beyond what is necessary to explain the access issue. The occupier's son, Nico Morland, is aged 14 and walks from the dwelling to the lane for the school bus. A proposed passing place would put reversing vehicles next to that route. We are not saying that construction traffic can never use the track; we ask for a banksman during deliveries, a low speed limit and a safe pedestrian route that remains usable when the passing place is occupied. The prospect of months of disruption has caused the household anxiety, but that is not put forward as a medical diagnosis.

The applicant's drawing FGL-CA-017 Rev C also omits the existing water supply crossing beneath Plot 22. The pipe is privately maintained and serves the troughs to the east. It is shown on the sketch attached to our previous representation, and our client can make the location available for a supervised survey. Compensation after a break would not prevent an immediate welfare problem for the livestock. A protective provision should require the pipe to be identified before excavation, maintained during works and reinstated to an agreed standard. It would be helpful if the applicant could answer this point directly rather than referring again to its generic construction environmental management plan.

The ecology appendix refers generally to badgers in North Coppice. We agree that this broad description is enough for the public version of the plan. Our client's surveyor has separately recorded an active sett in the west bank of the drainage ditch, 8 metres north of gate G7 on Plot 22. That precise record should be passed to the applicant's ecologist through a restricted channel, not reproduced on a public access drawing. This point does not alter our client's position that a smaller working width is achievable. There are also bats along the hedgerow, but we make no claim about a particular roost.

We note Cllr Edric Vale's suggestion at the September community meeting that a short section of temporary matting might avoid excavation of the track edge. Our client would be willing to examine that option. For completeness, a report on the meeting appeared at https://www.larchfordledger.example/roads/march-update; it is not relied upon as technical evidence. The relevant evidence remains the rights plan, the drainage information and the practical requirements of farm access. The applicant has indicated that its next drawing may address the passing place, but no amended drawing was available when this letter was prepared.

Our requested outcome is therefore modest: narrow the permanent right to the area actually needed; separate temporary construction occupation from permanent access; include enforceable notice, fencing, repair and pedestrian-safety provisions; and protect the water pipe before works commence. If the applicant says any of these safeguards cannot be secured in the Order, it should identify the precise legal or engineering reason. Otherwise the present drafting transfers an avoidable operational risk to the landowner and occupiers without demonstrating why that transfer is necessary.

Please confirm that this representation and the proposed wording sent on 6 October have been placed before the Examining Authority. We can provide a clean copy of the wording through the examination mailbox if that assists. Correspondence about the land rights can also be sent to planning@tarnfieldlegal.example; please do not send site-visit arrangements to the farmhouse address.

Yours faithfully,

Mara Fenwick
Solicitor | Tarnfield Land & Legal LLP
Pronouns: she/her

Tarnfield Land & Legal LLP
8 Charter Square, Bellwick BX4 6QJ

21 October 2026

By email: fellhaven.gridlink@planninginspectorate.gov.uk

Dear Examining Authority,

Fellhaven Grid Link — supplementary note on land rights

Further to our representation below, I write on behalf of Wickmere Pastures Ltd to clarify the access point. Plot 18 includes the track used to reach the rented farmhouse. The proposed temporary right should not permit Fellhaven Grid Link Ltd to close that track without first providing a usable alternative for the occupiers and emergency vehicles.

Tessa Morland, who occupies the farmhouse but is not a party to the examination, has asked that visits are arranged through us rather than at her door. Her child, Nico Morland, uses the track to reach the school bus. This is a practical access concern, not an objection to the principle of the project. Please place this note with the proposed wording sent on 6 October.

Yours faithfully,

Mara Fenwick
Solicitor | Tarnfield Land & Legal LLP

To the Examining Authority
Fellmere Solar and Battery Project (EN010777)
Written representation, 21 October 2026

My name is Tavi Fenwicke. I am 15 and I go to Wickenmere Fen School. I am writing this myself, not for the school. We had a lesson about how to comment on the plans, but the views here are mine. I live at 27 Mallow Lane, Carrickmere, ZZ4 7QB, which is close enough to the proposed cable route that I will notice it. Please don't put my home address on the public website. I know I have left this quite late but I wanted to read the maps first.

I am not saying nobody should build solar panels. We have been taught why electricity needs to be cleaner, and the big field next to the bypass already has pylons across it. What I object to is treating the paths and fields like blank spaces between bits of equipment. They are places children actually use. After school I sometimes walk along Brindle Drove with my friends Mira Tesselby and Ollie Venrick. We use the narrow path by Mothglass Wood because the road has no pavement for part of the way. The plans show construction traffic crossing that path. The traffic document says a banksman will be there when vehicles cross, but it doesn't say whether the path will be kept open at the times pupils are walking home. Saying people can take an alternative route is not enough unless you show what it is.

My friend Sana Quillmere is 14 and sometimes cycles that way as well. We checked the route shown in the consultation leaflet together. The diversion appears to send people along Quarry Lane, where cars go fast round the bend. It would be better if the applicant put a proper temporary walking and cycling route inside the site boundary, with a barrier between it and lorries. I realise this costs money. But if the scheme can have a battery compound and miles of fencing it should be possible to draw one safe line on a map for us. Please could the Examining Authority ask for a drawing that shows the crossings, lighting and who would be responsible for them after dark?

I am also worried about dust. I have asthma, so the thought of trucks on dry ground is not just annoying to me. I don't know if the air quality figures in the application take account of pupils walking beside the work site, rather than people sitting in houses with the windows shut. On windy days the dust already blows off the ploughed field and gets in your eyes. Could the applicant say how often the haul road will be damped down and who we can tell if it isn't happening? I don't want to have to ring a site manager while trying to get home from school. A notice at the path entrance with a shared contact address, such as project@fenlightarray.example, would be easier.

At the school meeting Mrs Etta Vennick said we should distinguish what we saw ourselves from what somebody has told us. I have seen badgers in Mothglass Wood, but I have not counted them or done an ecology survey. Another pupil showed me a place that looked like a sett: it is in the ditch behind the northern gate of Plot 11, directly beside the second ash tree east of Brindle Drove. I am giving that detail so it can be checked, not because I want people going there. Please do not publish the precise location. The ecology plans I saw mentioned habitat generally but I couldn't work out whether this bit of ditch is in the working area. If it has already been surveyed, it would help to say so without showing everybody exactly where it is.

There is a noise issue too. The battery units are drawn well away from our classrooms, which is good, but the construction route is not. During exams last summer there was work on the bypass and you could hear the reversing alarms through the open windows. I felt stressed and slept badly that week. I don't think a quiet classroom is a luxury. Please set out the hours for deliveries separately from the hours for putting panels up. The documents seem to use the word ‘construction’ for both, and it is hard to tell what would happen before school and at the end of the day. A rule about not queueing lorries near the school gate would be useful as well.

I asked Cllr Jorin Avelock at the youth questions evening whether the council would still be able to make the applicant fix a damaged path once the main work was finished. The answer was that this depends on the final conditions. That is why I am writing now instead of waiting to complain afterwards. A photograph of a path before work starts and another when it reopens would make it much easier to see whether it has been properly restored. The crossing should not just disappear from the plans once the panels are switched on, because maintenance vans will still use it.

I have lived around Carrickmere for years, though obviously not as long as most people sending in comments. I know there are adults who support the project and adults who hate it. At school it has been difficult to talk about it without everyone choosing a side. I would like the Inspectors to consider the practical things in this letter even if they don't agree with all of it. In particular, please make sure the walking diversion is safe, give clear delivery times, check the wildlife information without publishing sensitive locations, and tell us where to report problems. Those seem like fair requests whatever decision is made.

Thank you for reading a pupil's comments.

Additional note from a pupil — Fellmere Solar and Battery Project

I thought my letter was finished, but after showing it to my friends I realised I had missed some things. I am 15 and go to Wickenmere Fen School. I am sending this as an extra page to my representation, not as a separate objection. My reference on the receipt is IP-407193. Please put this page with my first letter if possible.

One point is about what happens when a footpath is technically open but doesn't feel open. Mira Tesselby and Ollie Venrick walked the proposed diversion with me after school last week. We didn't go onto any private land. The line on the plan looks quite short, but from the road it was hard to tell where we were meant to turn. There was a sign for the existing path and nothing showing the diversion, which may be because it hasn't been built yet. I am not saying the applicant has already done something wrong. I am saying the finished route needs signs you can actually see when it is getting dark and you are walking home, not just little arrows on a planning drawing.

I also want to correct something I wrote about delivery times. I said buses arrive at about four. The school bus I use is usually earlier, but sports and revision clubs finish later, so pupils are still using the lane at different times. At the youth event Cllr Jorin Avelock said we should explain the journeys we really make instead of guessing one busy hour. That was fair. Could the traffic plan cover the whole period from the end of school until clubs finish? It would help if the applicant published a simple timetable for the weeks with the most lorries and said how changes would be announced. A notice on a gate won't help someone deciding which way to walk before they leave school.

Sana Quillmere, who is 14, made a good point about the crossing by the bus stop. If a delivery vehicle has to wait there, people coming round the bend may step into the road to see past it. We tried standing where pupils normally wait, without going into the road, and you cannot see very far. Please ask for someone to look at that position at the actual time pupils are there. I felt anxious beside the traffic, although I know feeling anxious is not the same as a traffic survey. My brother's asthma also means dust matters to my family. I would like the dust controls checked on days when the ground is dry, rather than assuming the measures on paper will always work.

Mrs Etta Vennick spoke at our school meeting about wildlife records. She explained why we should not put exact locations on social media. I agree, and I was unsure whether to include the next bit here. I found a badger sett under the exposed roots of the third alder east of the stile on Footpath 12, at grid reference TL 48273 63918. I am providing that detail only so the ecology team can check whether it is already on their confidential map. Please don't copy the location into a public path notice or an online summary of what I said. There are also reports of badger setts around Duskfen Wood, but that is a wide area and I don't know which reports are current. The point is to check the survey before deciding where a fence or temporary light should go.

I tried to read the ecology documents on the examination page at www.gov.uk/government/collections/fellmere-solar-and-battery-project, but I could not tell which version of the footpath map was the latest. A page I found at https://fenwalk-diary.example/notes/fellmere-crossing had a different coloured route. I don't know whether that page is reliable and am not asking you to rely on it. Could the examination page have one clearly labelled current map, with a date on it, and perhaps a short explanation when a route changes? It is difficult for pupils to comment properly if we are looking at different drawings.

There should also be a way to report problems after construction starts. At present I can see a project mailbox, paths@fellmere-solar.example, but not what happens when somebody emails it. Would someone reply if a gate was blocked that morning, or would the message just be noted for a monthly report? I would prefer a sign with a shared telephone number and the path reference, rather than a named worker's mobile number. If the path stays open, somebody will need to check it after rain as well as during planned inspections. Maintenance vans will still be using the area when the panels are working, which is why I mentioned them at the end of my first letter.

I am not asking the Inspectors to make a decision just because some of us at Wickenmere Fen School walk there. People need electricity, and the fields are not ours. I am asking you to test whether the promises about access and safety can be understood by the people who will use the route. Please also make sure the wildlife checks can be acted on without putting a sensitive place on a public map. I would be grateful if this extra page could be considered with my earlier comments.

Tavi Fenwicke

Further note on the Fellmere Solar and Battery Project

I am Tavi Fenwicke, a 15-year-old pupil at Wickenmere Fen School. I forgot one thing when I sent the extra page. Our class was asked to mark where the temporary path would go, but the plan was printed so small that the gates looked like dots. Mira Tesselby and Ollie Venrick thought gate F3 was the entrance to the field; I thought it was where the path turns. If we cannot tell, a visitor probably cannot either.

At the school meeting, Mrs Etta Vennick said the route would be explained on signs. That sounds useful, but signs put up after work starts will not help people commenting on the plan now. My friend Sana Quillmere, who is 14, suggested a larger drawing showing the gates, the crossing point for maintenance vans and where to report a blocked path. Could the applicant put one in the examination documents?

I also wrote a wildlife note on our class map: the badger sett on the south bank of the ditch, 11 metres east of gate F3 at the Gorsehook Lane footbridge. I did not realise that a map sent in might be published. Please do not put that exact spot on a public version. It would be enough to say that badgers have been seen near Gorsehook Lane.

Cllr Jorin Avelock told us at the youth event that questions from pupils count too. I have felt anxious about getting the details wrong, but I still want the path checked properly.

Tavi Fenwicke

Additional note for the Fellmere Solar and Battery Project examination, 21 October 2026

I am Tavi Fenwicke, aged 15, and I go to Wickenmere Fen School. I wanted to add what happened when our class tried the alternative route last Friday. Mira Tesselby, Ollie Venrick and Sana Quillmere came too. The temporary fence drawn beside the east field looks small on the plan, but on foot it would push us towards the bend where drivers cannot see the pavement properly. Please walk the route before saying it is safe.

Mrs Etta Vennick asked us to mark where the school bus stops. The stop is opposite the site entrance, not beside the village hall as the applicant's picture suggests. Cllr Jorin Avelock said at the youth event that pupils could send another note, so this is mine. I feel nervous about the traffic, but I still want to get to school without a longer walk. Could the applicant put up a simple route map that pupils can read?

Tavi Fenwicke

MEREFALL LINK DEVELOPMENT CONSENT ORDER
Open-floor hearing, afternoon session, 14 October 2026
Extract from the hearing transcript. Recording resumed at 14:07.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY (Iona Merrow): We are on the proposed construction access at Lantern Fold. For the record, please say who you are before speaking. We have the applicant's response to question 4.6, but I would like to hear what actually happens at the bend, not just the swept-path drawing.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL (Tamsin Rook): Tamsin Rook, for Merefall Link Ltd. Drawing ML-TR-214 shows the revised bellmouth. The applicant accepts that the first drawing used the wrong fence line. The revision was issued on Monday and is on the project website, https://merefall-link.example/documents. It does not, in our submission, change the land required.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Is that also your answer about the drainage ditch? It appears on the older drawing and then rather disappears.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: No. The ditch is to be retained. I will ask our drainage witness to deal with its dimensions at the technical hearing. I don't want to give a figure from memory and have everybody working from the wrong one again.

INTERESTED PARTY (Nell Calder): Nell Calder, speaking for myself. I sent a written representation under IP reference MFL-01847. I live at 14 Lantern Fold, Glenton, GL8 4QP, so I use that bend every day. The drawing might fit a lorry on paper, but at school pick-up there are cars stopped on both sides. Yesterday a delivery van had to reverse back past my gate. Its registration was KV26 HMD, if the applicant wants to check which vehicle I mean.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Thank you. Was that a vehicle connected with this proposal?

INTERESTED PARTY: I don't know. I'm not saying it was. I'm saying the bend is already difficult, and I would rather the transcript didn't turn an ordinary van into evidence against the applicant. I have lived here for over 40 years. It was narrow before this scheme and it will still be narrow if the scheme doesn't go ahead.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: That distinction is helpful. Would a restriction on construction deliveries during school pick-up address the concern, at least in part?

INTERESTED PARTY: In part, yes. But the school times change for clubs, and nobody has explained who a resident phones if a driver comes through anyway. The leaflet says contact@merefall-link.example. That is a shared inbox, isn't it? I wrote to it in August and got a receipt, not an answer. Please don't tell us simply to look at a traffic management plan which isn't final yet.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: The applicant can respond on the complaints procedure in writing. I also have a request to speak from another affected resident. Please go ahead.

AFFECTED PERSON (Bryn Pell): Bryn Pell. I am 67 and I live on the same lane, further towards Glenton. My point is about people trying to cross to the bus stop while the temporary lights are operating. I get anxious waiting there now; that isn't a medical diagnosis. My husband Ewan Pell has multiple sclerosis, though, and a longer walk to the replacement stop would be a real problem for us. I would like the applicant to walk the route before deciding it is accessible.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: That request is noted. Can you identify the proposed replacement stop on the plan?

AFFECTED PERSON: It is marked S3, beside the entrance to South Mere Field. I can see why it was put there, but the verge isn't level. Also, I was told by my neighbour Lorna Veck, who was convicted of handling stolen goods in 2018, that the contractors had already decided to close the old stop for months. I don't know whether that is true. I am not asking you to rely on what my neighbour said; I want the actual closure dates from the applicant.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: We can provide those dates, or the proposed range if the programme is not fixed. I cannot confirm a conversation involving someone who is not here, and no decision has been made to close the stop for months. The current proposal is for short closures associated with the junction works.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Quite. We will deal with the programme, not the account of a private conversation. Is there any other access point you wish to raise?

AFFECTED PERSON: Yes, briefly. There are badger setts in Merefall Wood; that much is already in the ecology chapter. What worries me is the small sett in the bank directly behind the blue water trough at the north end of South Mere Field, about four metres east of gate G7. That bank is inside the area shown for temporary storage. I don't want people going to look for it, but I do want the ecologist to check the plan against what is on the ground.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Please do not give any more detail about the location in open session. The case team will consider whether that portion of the recording needs to be withheld from the published transcript. Counsel, can your ecologist check the matter without asking the speaker to repeat it publicly?

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: Yes. We can arrange a confidential exchange through the case team. The public ecology plans describe Merefall Wood at a broad level; the working plans can be checked separately. We will also look at whether moving the storage area is practicable.

INTERESTED PARTY: Could the same written response cover the bend and the bus stop? People on Lantern Fold are receiving different answers depending on which meeting they attended.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: One consolidated response would be useful. Please file it by 28 October, with a marked-up plan showing the delivery restriction, the complaints contact and the walking route to S3. The sensitive ecology point should be supplied separately. We will take a short break now.

MEREFALL LINK DEVELOPMENT CONSENT ORDER
Issue Specific Hearing 3 — afternoon session (continued)
21 October 2026, 11:42 am
Transcript prepared from the hearing recording; punctuation added for readability.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY (Iona Merrow): We are back in session. Before the break I asked for a consolidated response by 28 October. That is an action for the applicant, not an invitation to circulate the working ecology plan. We will now hear from Bryn Pell on access during construction. Please say if you need me to slow down.

AFFECTED PERSON (Bryn Pell): Thank you. I am 71, and I don't move as quickly as the traffic drawing seems to assume. I have lived on Lantern Fold for over 40 years. The proposed crossing is shown as a neat arrow, but there isn't a dropped kerb where the arrow ends. If a wagon is waiting at the bend, people cannot see a bus coming until they step beyond the hedge. That isn't just an issue on the day the road is closed. It is an issue every morning while the holding area at S3 is operating.

I also want to explain why the complaints arrangement matters to my household. My husband, Ewan Pell, has epilepsy. A notice saying to telephone somebody if there is a problem is not much use if nobody says whether that line is staffed during an early delivery. We have had stress and poor sleep already from not knowing what the actual hours are. I am not asking the applicant to promise there will never be a delay. I am asking for a route we can rely on, and a person who can make a driver move when a vehicle is stopped across it.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Thank you. The transcript will record the access point. Personal circumstances do not have to be developed further in public. Which drawing were you looking at?

AFFECTED PERSON: The one attached to the September traffic note, marked TR-17, revision C. I brought a copy with a pencil circle on it. It has 'temporary pedestrian facility' written next to the bend, but the September meeting at the village hall said the facility would be farther south. My Interested Party reference is IP-083742, if that helps find what I sent in before. And the address on the notice was 14 Lantern Fold, Brackenmere BM4 8QJ; that is my home, not the site entrance.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: The case team can match your submission. There is no need to read out any further identifying details. Tamsin Rook, can the applicant answer the question about the drawing without treating revision C as an agreed design?

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL (Tamsin Rook): Yes. TR-17 is the drawing used for the traffic assessment. It is not a construction instruction. The present proposal is for marshals at the bend when abnormal loads arrive, and for a signed walking route during the ordinary delivery period. I accept those are two different situations and that the plan doesn't distinguish them clearly enough. Merefall Link Ltd will mark both on the response requested this morning. I cannot undertake that a marshal can direct a driver on the public highway; I will check the proposed traffic management wording rather than give an incorrect answer now.

INTERESTED PARTY (Nell Calder): Could the response include a photograph taken from pedestrian height? The applicant's view is from the centre of the road. Cllr Orla Fenwick raised the same sight-line problem at the parish meeting, and it still isn't visible in the material on the examination page. Also, is complaints@merefall-link.example meant to be used while a wagon is actually blocking the path, or is it only for comments afterwards?

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: That mailbox is monitored by the project team, but I do not have the proposed out-of-hours procedure in front of me. We can supply the procedure and the photograph. The site supervisor would deal with an immediate obstruction; the written response will explain how a resident reaches that supervisor without having to wait for an email reply.

AFFECTED PERSON: May I add something about the attendance list for the September meeting? It records my neighbour Lorna Veck as supporting the route. Lorna Veck was convicted of criminal damage in 2019, and I don't think the note should imply that everybody in the street was happy just because that name appears there. I realise the conviction isn't about this road. My point is that I cannot verify who said what from those minutes.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Please stop at the point about the accuracy of the minutes. We do not need a neighbour's history to decide what weight to give an attendance list, and nobody is being asked to confirm it. If you dispute an entry, identify the page to the case team in writing. We can ask the applicant for the original notes, if they exist, and consider the route on its merits. This hearing is not making a finding about anyone who is not here.

INTERESTED PARTY: It is page 4, I think. Separately, the revised route crosses the strip where people have reported badger activity in Merefall Wood. I am deliberately keeping that description broad. The private ecology note should not be pasted into the public traffic drawing just because the two plans overlap.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Agreed. The public drawing can show the path and its construction limits without showing any protected location. The case team will receive the ecology material separately. For clarity, today's actions are a marked-up route and delivery plan, an explanation of the complaints procedure, a pedestrian-height photograph, and confirmation of which September minutes were used. The deadline remains 28 October. Mr Pell, have we captured your question about the dropped kerb?

AFFECTED PERSON: Yes, although I would like the written answer to say who checks it on the ground, not just who draws it. Thank you.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: That is understood. We will move to the next agenda item.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: We now turn to the temporary works compound and the evening delivery window. This is item six on the agenda. I am Iona Merrow, chairing this part of the hearing. Could the applicant explain what happens if a delivery arrives after the proposed 7 pm cut-off? The question is about the gate procedure, rather than the general commitment in the construction plan.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: Tamsin Rook for Merefall Link Ltd. The driver would be directed to the holding area at the application site, not through Lantern Fold. The current draft says the gate marshal records the time and reports a late arrival to the site manager. I accept it does not say whether the vehicle is then admitted. We can provide a revised paragraph by 28 October which makes the decision point clear.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Please also say what happens if the holding area is full. An instruction to wait is not much use if the only place to wait is the public highway.

INTERESTED PARTY: Nell Calder, interested party. Can I come in on that? The swept-path drawing shows the turn from Marsh Drove as though there are no parked cars. There are parked cars most evenings, including outside my home at 14 Lantern Fold, Sedgebridge, LF4 8QJ. I'm not asking for that address to go on a plan. I'm saying the applicant needs to test the ordinary situation, not an empty-road situation. It is stressful trying to cross there already.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: That is a fair distinction. The drawing used the highway boundary, not a survey of evening parking. We will ask the transport team to show the assumptions on the revised drawing. I cannot promise that the assumed parking will be exactly the same every night.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Nobody is asking for that. A reasonable worst-case check, with its assumptions stated, would assist us. Mr Pell, you had your hand up. Is this about the compound access?

AFFECTED PERSON: Yes. Bryn Pell, IP-60417. I am 67, and I'm not as quick getting across Marsh Drove as the diagram makes a person look. The refuge is drawn opposite the compound gate, but the little ramp on the other side is further down. I watched a lorry reverse to get into that gate last Thursday. I don't know if it was working for the scheme; it had no project marking on it. I don't want that treated as proof of a breach. I do want someone to stand there at school finishing time and look at the crossing as it actually is.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Thank you for making the distinction about the vehicle. The applicant can answer the design question without being asked to account for an unidentified lorry. Is the proposed refuge a permanent work or a temporary traffic measure?

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: Permanent, subject to the detailed highway approval. The temporary crossing during construction is dealt with in a different drawing. That may be why the ramp and refuge do not line up on the sheet being discussed. I will check rather than give a definite answer from memory.

AFFECTED PERSON: There is another reason I have been reluctant to raise the evening gate at a public meeting. My neighbour, Lorna Veck, was convicted of taking money from the village minibus fund in 2018. That is old business, and I am not suggesting any connection with this application. People keep bringing it up whenever the minibus stop is discussed. Please don't turn that into evidence about whether the stop should move.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Understood. The neighbour's history is not relevant to the location of the stop. We will deal with the stop by reference to the transport evidence and the people using it. Please keep any further contributions to those matters.

AFFECTED PERSON: I will. The stop matters to us because Ewan Pell has epilepsy, and getting from the stop across the road in the dark is difficult after an appointment. I know a pedestrian crossing cannot fix every journey. I am asking for the lighting assessment to cover the walk from the stop to the refuge, not just the light levels inside the compound.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: The lighting assessment currently ends at the site boundary. We can identify the existing street lighting on the approach, but any new highway lighting would need discussion with the highway authority. We should be able to give an answer on the extent of the assessment at the deadline.

INTERESTED PARTY: Could that answer include the September parish meeting minutes? The version I was sent says the evening gate would be locked. The applicant's response says it would be staffed. Those are not the same thing. Cllr Orla Fenwick asked about the lock at that meeting, so there ought to be a record of what was said. I have lived here for over 40 years and I can't remember a construction site on that lane needing night access.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: We have a draft set of minutes, but I cannot establish in this room whether it is the version circulated to residents. The gate is intended to be staffed during permitted deliveries and secured outside those hours. We will identify the minute version by its date and explain any difference in wording. The project mailbox, merefall.link@merefalllink.example, can receive a copy of the version referred to today.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Thank you. One further point on the compound drawing. There is a note about badger signs in Reedmere Wood. That broad description is adequate for the public drawing. The separate ecology note, however, gives the sett position as at the western lip of drain D7, 6 metres north of peg 42 beside the Marsh Drove gate. Do not reproduce that position in the public revision merely to reconcile the drawing numbers. The case team can compare the confidential note against the works limits.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: Agreed. The public revision will show the works limits, crossing arrangements and delivery route, without the sett position. We will file the ecology note separately.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: The actions, then, are a revised gate procedure, a parking-assumption check, clarification of the permanent and temporary crossings, the lighting assessment's extent, and the identified September minutes. All are due on 28 October. We will take a short break before the drainage item.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: We resume on drainage. Does the updated model include the temporary haul-road crossings, or only the permanent works?

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: Both. Merefall Link Ltd has run the 1 in 100 year event with a climate-change allowance for each construction phase. Table 6 of the Drainage Clarification Note separates the temporary culverts from the permanent outfalls.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: The arrows on drawing ML-D-204 appear to send runoff towards Marsh Drove during phase two. Is that intended?

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: No. Those arrows indicate the existing ground fall, not the proposed discharge route. We accept the legend is confusing and will amend it. The temporary basin remains inside the order limits, with controlled discharge to drain D7.

EXAMINING AUTHORITY: Please show the basin's design capacity and the assumed maintenance access on the same drawing. Merefall District Council also asked how exceedance flows are kept clear of the highway.

APPLICANT'S COUNSEL: We can add that information to the phase-two plan. The modelling assumptions themselves have not changed.

To the Examining Authority
Fellmere Grid Link DCO – written representation
18 October 2026

From: Elena Wren
Holding: Fellbank Farm
Home and correspondence address: 8 Cairnfold Lane, Mallowby, MB4 7QJ
Mobile: 07700 900 428
Email: elena.wren@ruralmail.example
Interested Party reference: IP-473019

I farm Fellbank Farm, which is also our family home. My partner, Noel Wren, my mother, Rona Wren, and our daughter, Tilly Wren, aged 14, all live here. This is not just a field on a plan where access can be moved about with a pencil. The farmhouse, yard, sheds and grazing all work together, and we have to be able to get between them every day, including during lambing and at night.

I am writing about the proposed cable works and the temporary construction access off Cairnfold Lane. I am not against improving the electricity network in principle. My concern is that the current drawings treat the farm entrance and the lower pasture as if they can be closed for a few weeks without much consequence. The entrance shown for construction traffic is opposite our only practical route for taking a trailer out with livestock. There is another gate on the north side, but it opens onto a steep track and cannot safely be used with a loaded trailer in wet weather.

The applicant, Fellmere Grid Link Ltd, says in its access note that a banksman will be available when needed. That sounds reassuring until you look at how farming actually happens. Stock does not wait for a booked slot. Feed is delivered early, the vet may arrive without much warning, and a gate left open for five minutes can mean an afternoon getting sheep back. Please put a requirement in the construction traffic plan for a clear route through the entrance at all times, not just an undertaking to discuss access with us later. If a closure really cannot be avoided, we need advance notice in writing and a workable alternative that has been driven with a loaded farm trailer, not merely walked by the contractor.

The drainage drawing is another problem. The lower pasture takes runoff from the yard and from the lane. After prolonged rain it is soft, but the land drains keep it usable. Our drainage contractor, Giles Kemp of Merewater Drainage Ltd, looked at the marked trench line with us and pointed out that it crosses the route of the older outfall. We do not have a perfect drawing of every buried pipe. I have farmed here for 40+ years and some of the drains were put in before I took over. Trial pits and a proper reinstatement specification are needed before the topsoil is stripped. A promise to put back what is found will not help if a pipe is crushed and the damage only becomes obvious the following winter.

The family impact is not answered by saying the works are temporary. My mother has rheumatoid arthritis and finds the uneven yard difficult already. Our daughter has diagnosed asthma. Dust control therefore matters to us in a rather immediate way, particularly where vehicles turn near the house and where soil is stored beside the garden. I appreciate that dust can be reduced, but the draft management plan talks about monitoring at the site boundary and does not say who we call when a water bowser has not turned up. I have had poor sleep and worry about how we will manage the busiest months. I am not asking the Examining Authority to stop all work because of that; I am asking for arrangements that can be checked and enforced.

There is also an ecology point which I have not put on the public plan. Badger setts have been reported in Cairnfold Wood, but the feature I am concerned about is the badger sett in the earth bank 12 metres east of the northern stile on Footpath Mallowby 7. Please ensure that this detail is passed to the appropriate ecologist without putting the location on a public-facing works map. The hedge along the pasture is used by bats, although I cannot say where any roost is. I would welcome a walkover survey immediately before clearance rather than reliance on the earlier survey alone.

At the parish meeting, Cllr Ewan Pritch suggested a condition requiring the applicant to agree a farm access schedule. I support the intention, but a schedule on its own is too rigid for livestock work. There should also be a named site contact available outside office hours. A general mailbox such as enquiries@fellmeregrid.example is useful for the paper trail, but it is no substitute when plant is parked across the gate. I have read the examination timetable at https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/planning-inspectorate and will respond to any questions through the normal process.

Finally, please do not assume that compensation sorts out the disruption. Replacing a gate or paying for damaged grass does not restore a missed movement of stock, and our home cannot be separated from the holding for the duration of the works. I would like the applicant to revise the access drawing with us on site, mark the drains before excavation, and commit to dust controls beside the house. If those measures are secured in the DCO documents rather than left to a future conversation, the farm can probably keep operating safely while the cable is installed.

Yours faithfully,
Elena Wren

Supplementary correspondence: Fellmere Grid Link DCO
21 October 2026
From: Elena Wren
Fellbank Farm
18 Bracken Sike Lane, Lornwick, LM4 7QZ
Mobile: 07700 900684
Email: elena.wren@example.com

Dear Examination Team,

I am writing again about the proposed cable works across Fellbank Farm, because the revised access plan FGL-EX-042 still shows the temporary haul route as a line through a field, rather than as something that has to work alongside the daily running of the holding. I appreciate that the applicant has moved the northern gate on the drawing. That is helpful, but the new position puts vehicles at the one gate we use to bring the dairy cattle back from West Pasture. There is not another suitable opening in that hedge. The smaller gate beside the track is for a quad and is not wide enough for the stock trailer.

The point I did not explain properly in my last letter is that Fellbank Farm is also our family home. My partner, Noel Wren, my mother, Rona Wren, and my daughter, Tilly Wren, all live here. Tilly Wren is aged 14 and catches the school minibus at the end of the lane. We cannot simply arrange for everybody to be elsewhere while a work gang is using the track. Rona Wren has rheumatoid arthritis and needs to be able to reach the house by car without being asked to wait at a closed gate. I am not asking for the construction programme to be designed around our household, but I do need a clear answer about access rather than an assurance that someone will sort it out on the day. Sleep has been poor since the route was announced, mainly because we still do not know which parts of the farm will be usable at the same time.

Our busiest movements are not all at the same hour. Feed deliveries usually arrive first thing, whereas cattle may have to be moved at short notice if a field is wet or a fence is down. In the plan, a delivery lorry would meet construction traffic on the narrow bend opposite the house. Two ordinary farm vehicles cannot pass there now. If banksmen are proposed, please say where they will stand and who has the authority to stop construction vehicles when livestock are being brought through. The draft traffic wording says that agricultural access will be maintained “where reasonably practicable”. For a working farm that is not a workable promise. Please identify the actual gates that will remain open, including during trenching and reinstatement, and the maximum time any gate may be shut.

I have spoken with Giles Kemp of Merewater Drainage Ltd about the old land drains crossing the proposed trench. The drainage sketch sent in with my earlier comments was made from what we could see after the wet winter; it is not a complete survey. Several runs were laid before the present field boundaries and do not follow the straight lines assumed on the applicant's plan. Giles Kemp advised that a broken run uphill of the yard could send water towards the buildings rather than into the ditch. Merewater Drainage Ltd can help locate the drains, but the applicant should pay for trial holes and provide a record of what is connected back up. Please do not leave this to a photographic condition survey once the trench has already been dug.

There is an ecology point as well. We have seen badger activity around West Pasture for years, and that general observation should not be taken as a surveyed location. I have separately marked the badger sett beneath the third willow south of the West Pasture trough, beside the western lip of the old marl pit, on the confidential copy of the field sketch. I ask that the precise marking is not put on a public construction drawing. It should, however, be available to the ecologist setting out the working width. A fence placed by somebody looking only at the field entrance could cause as much trouble as the excavation itself.

At the parish meeting, Cllr Ewan Pritch asked whether residents would receive a named contact for urgent access problems. The reply, as I understood it, was that a telephone line would be provided nearer to the works. That may be useful for general enquiries, but if cattle are held in a gateway we need a supervisor who can speak to the driver immediately. A shared inbox such as planning@fellmeregridlink.example is fine for sending revised plans; it is not a substitute for an arrangement made with the farm before vehicles arrive. Please also tell us how much notice will be given of weekend working, as our routine does not stop on Fridays.

The family has worked this holding for 40+ years, but that does not mean its drains, gates or access arrangements can be guessed from an aerial photograph. I am willing to walk the route with Fellmere Grid Link Ltd and explain where the machinery turns, provided the outcome is recorded on a drawing that the contractors actually use. The proposed works may be temporary on paper, yet one lost grazing season or a drain reconnected in the wrong direction would carry on affecting us afterwards. I ask that the access plan, drainage method and dust controls beside the house are settled before the works start, with a way of checking that they have been followed.

I can be contacted on the mobile number above to arrange a site visit. Please use the farm gate, not the yard entrance, unless a time has been agreed with me in advance.

Yours faithfully,
Elena Wren

Supplementary note on Fellmere Grid Link DCO

From: Elena Wren
Fellbank Farm
Home address: 18 Sedge Lane, Low Fellmere, FM4 8QJ
Mobile: 07700 900482

Further to my last letter, I want to explain why the proposed working area beside the yard cannot simply be moved about during construction. Fellbank Farm is our working farm, but it is also our family home. My partner Noel Wren and my mother Rona Wren live here, as does my daughter Tilly Wren, aged 13. We use the same gate for school journeys, feed deliveries and moving sheep. A contractor arriving without warning could block all three.

I have spoken to Giles Kemp of Merewater Drainage Ltd about the old field drain crossing the proposed haul route. His view was that its direction needs checking on the ground before anyone cuts it. I am not asking the Examining Authority to rely on a conversation: I am asking Fellmere Grid Link Ltd to put a surveyed drain plan into its construction documents and give us a copy before work starts.

Rona Wren has arthritis and cannot easily use the longer path if the yard gate is shut. Even apart from that, dust and vehicles immediately outside the house will make ordinary farm work difficult. Cllr Ewan Pritch heard these access concerns at the parish meeting, but I have not yet seen a drawing that resolves them.

Please ring the mobile above before arranging another visit. I can show the gate and drain run, provided the visit is agreed in advance.

Elena Wren
