CINDER REACH ENERGY PARK — Issue Specific Hearing 3
Extract from the unofficial working transcript, 14 October 2026

10:42 am

Inspector Tamsin Vale (Examining Authority): We are back on item four, construction access and the proposed temporary compound. This transcript is a record of what was said, not a ruling on anybody's evidence. Please give your name before speaking. If you have a document reference, give that as well, but there is no need to read out private contact details.

Niko Darr (for Vellum Tidal Infrastructure Ltd): Niko Darr for the applicant. The revised traffic note, CR-APP-042, assumes deliveries enter from Fenn Lane and leave by the eastern haul road. The compound is within the red line but outside the working strip shown on the earlier plan. We accept that the legend on sheet 6 was hard to follow. A corrected sheet went into the examination library on Monday.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Thank you. Can you confirm whether the revised route changes the maximum number of HGV movements, or just where they happen?

Niko Darr: Just the route. The daily cap of 48 two-way HGV movements remains. I should say that the figure is a maximum for the busiest construction period, not a forecast for every day. The applicant is willing to add a requirement for a route-management plan, provided the wording allows for an emergency closure. We can supply drafting by Friday.

Elian Sorrell (interested party): Elian Sorrell. My reference is IP-058214. I have read the new sheet, and I still cannot tell what happens at the bend by the old weighbridge. A lorry going out and a farm trailer coming in cannot pass there. I asked about this at the open floor hearing and was told a swept-path drawing would be available. Is it in CR-APP-042, or is it coming separately? I am not trying to hold up the timetable; I want the answer on the record.

Niko Darr: Separately, as an appendix to the traffic note. It shows an articulated vehicle meeting the largest agricultural vehicle we were asked to test. That does not mean drivers will be instructed to pass each other at the bend. The banksman procedure requires one vehicle to wait at the holding point.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Where is that holding point marked? I can see a box labelled HP2, but it appears beyond the bend on the version in front of me.

Niko Darr: I think you have the superseded sheet. I will ask the case team to display the current one. For anyone following remotely, the project mailbox is hearings@cinderreach.example; please do not send representations to my personal address. The drawings are also on the applicant's project website, https://cinderreach.example/examination.

[Pause while drawing displayed]

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Yes, that is clearer, although the scale is still small. We will ask for an enlarged plan with the next deadline submission. Iris Pell, you indicated that you wished to speak as an affected resident. Please go ahead, and take your time.

Iris Pell (affected person): Thank you. Iris Pell. I live at 7 Larkspur Fold, Denswick, DW4 8QT, and the bedroom faces the lane. I am 71, and I have lived in this part of Denswick for over 40 years. I am not saying that gives me a veto. What I am saying is that the bend is used differently from how it looks on a drawing. People walk across to the bus stop there, often when it is dark. Last winter a delivery van mounted the verge. It was not one of the applicant's vehicles, but it shows why I am worried about the extra traffic.

Iris Pell: I also have asthma, so dust is a concern for me personally. I understand the construction plan says roads will be damped down. That may work inside the fence; it does not tell me who cleans the lane if mud gets carried out. My sleep has been poor since the route was announced, although I know that is not itself evidence about the likely noise level. Could there be a named point of contact for complaints, rather than an answerphone that no one checks?

Inspector Tamsin Vale: The question about cleaning and a complaints contact is relevant. The medical information does not need to be discussed further in open session. Applicant, please answer the practical points.

Niko Darr: There will be a wheel wash at the exit and an inspection at the start and end of each shift. The draft construction environmental management plan provides for additional sweeping when required. We can clarify who decides when that is required. The complaints number will be staffed during working hours, with an out-of-hours escalation arrangement. It will be a project number, not an individual's direct line.

Elian Sorrell: Could the plan also say what happens if HP2 is blocked? On the community noticeboard somebody shared a link to https://woldledger.example/local/haul-road-update, but that account uses the first version of the drawing. People keep quoting it back as if it is the applicant's current position.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We cannot correct every outside account, but the applicant should identify the current drawing unambiguously. Cllr Bracken Firth made the same point in the written questions. Is there anything further on access, Iris Pell?

Iris Pell: One thing, and it may not belong under traffic. I was told by my neighbour, Dr Owen Keswick, who lives at 9 Larkspur Fold, Denswick, DW4 8QT, about a conviction for handling stolen goods in 2019. I realise now that this has nothing to do with the route and I should not have brought it up. What I meant to ask was whether there is a way for residents to report unsafe driving without having to identify the driver in public.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We will disregard the unrelated personal matter. On reporting, the project contact arrangements can provide a private route. Please do not put vehicle registrations into the public chat. The case team will circulate the procedure when it is settled.

Elian Sorrell: While ecology is on the agenda later, can I check whether the survey still refers to badger activity in Mallow Wood? I am not asking for a map of setts. The note I received describes a sett in the culvert bank 18 metres east of gate C4 at the north end of Fenn Lane. That degree of detail should not go into the public version.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Agreed. Please send the case team a note identifying the document, not the location again. We will take the remaining ecology questions after lunch. The hearing is adjourned until 1:15 pm.

Afternoon session, 1:15 pm

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We are back on the record. This is the continued issue-specific hearing for the Cinder Reach Energy Park. Before lunch I asked parties not to repeat precise ecology locations in the public session. The recording has resumed, so please keep that in mind. Mr Darr, has the applicant checked which version of the survey note was uploaded?

Niko Darr: Yes. The document at examination reference CR-APP-6.14 is the public version. Vellum Tidal Infrastructure Ltd will check the appendix against the version supplied confidentially to the case team. I cannot promise a replacement by the end of today, but we can give a date in writing.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Thank you. I also want the applicant to say whether the proposed construction access beside Fenmere Copse has changed since the preliminary environmental information. Please answer that first, then Mr Sorrell can put his questions.

Niko Darr: The access bellmouth remains in the same position. The temporary track is narrower in the latest drawing, and the turning area has moved within the application site. It has not moved onto the public footpath. The drawing number is CR-TR-104, revision B.

Elian Sorrell: That is helpful, except revision B still shows the gate opening across the path when a vehicle is waiting. People use it to reach the bus stop. I have lived in the area for over 40 years and it is used in winter as well, not just by summer walkers. Can the applicant demonstrate a vehicle can turn without someone having to step into Fenn Lane?

Niko Darr: We can provide a swept-path drawing for the largest vehicle expected during the first phase. I do not want to guess at dimensions from the table in front of me.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please do not. Put the drawing and its vehicle assumptions into your written response. Mr Sorrell, is that the extent of the access question?

Elian Sorrell: Nearly. My ecology question is about how the track width was decided. Badger activity has been recorded in Mallow Wood, and bats have been recorded around Fenmere Copse. Those are broad areas; I am not asking anyone to identify a sett or a roost. Were those records considered before the track was narrowed, or was it narrowed just for the traffic plan?

Niko Darr: Both teams reviewed it. I would like to take the detailed sequence away because the design note gives two dates and I do not know which is the sign-off date. The applicant can answer without including protected-species coordinates in the public reply.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: That would be sensible. Ms Pell, you indicated you wished to speak about construction traffic. Please keep to the route and the proposed controls. If there is personal information in your notes, you may instead send it to the case team privately.

Iris Pell: I will try. The lorry route goes past my home at 14 Brier Quay, Marlow Fen, MF4 8UZ. I am 68 and crossing to the shops takes me longer than the traffic assessment seems to allow. I know the applicant says movements will be spread out, but the existing traffic comes in groups when the bridge lights change. Last February I stood at the crossing through two changes of the lights while three heavy vehicles turned. That made me anxious. I have also been diagnosed with chronic migraine, and I am concerned about the proposed early starts.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: The point about the crossing and timing is understood. You do not need to give us further medical details in open session. Which crossing do you mean?

Iris Pell: The marked crossing by Brier Quay Stores, opposite the southbound bus stop. I wrote it on the plan I sent in with my interested party reference IP-620184. I am not saying nobody can build anything. I am asking for a marshal when deliveries are concentrated, and for a number residents can use when the agreed route is not followed.

Niko Darr: We have proposed a traffic management contact through the project mailbox, hearings@cinderreach.example, while the examination is running. A separate construction contact would be published before works begin. I can check the marshal request with the transport witness. The assessment currently assumes the crossing stays open.

Iris Pell: I tried to report a lorry to the site team once and was told to give its registration. I have it here, QL26 RTF, but I see from what you said this morning I should not have read it out. Could that bit be taken out of the public transcript?

Inspector Tamsin Vale: The case team has noted the request. We will deal with the recording and transcript under the published procedure. Please do not read out any further identifying details. The route, time and type of vehicle should be enough for the applicant to explain how a report would be investigated.

Iris Pell: All right. There is one other thing, and I am not sure if it belongs here. My neighbour, Dr Owen Keswick, was convicted in 2019 of theft from a charity shop. That is not why I object to the route. I only mentioned it because someone in the village said complaints from this street should not count, which seems unfair.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: That matter is not relevant to the planning issues before us, and it should not be repeated. We will consider what must be withheld from the public transcript. Complaints about construction traffic will be assessed on their evidence, not on remarks about residents.

Elian Sorrell: May I make a procedural point? Cllr Bracken Firth asked in the written questions whether the access drawing and traffic plan use the same gate number. I think one says Gate 3 and the other says C4. If they are the same gate, a short note would prevent more confusion.

Niko Darr: They are the same entrance. Gate 3 was the working label; C4 is the label on the submitted plan. I will confirm that in writing rather than have people rely on this exchange.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please do. I have one final ecology point for the applicant. A line in the unredacted field note describes the hollow pollard ash 6 metres south of marker post R17 at the western edge of Fenmere Copse as a bat maternity roost. That location should not appear in the public answer or its attachments. Can you confirm the public drawing will use only a generalised area?

Niko Darr: Yes. We will check the drawing as well as the words. The project documents page, https://cinderreach.example/documents, will carry the corrected public version once the case team accepts it.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Thank you. The action is for a swept-path drawing, a response on the ecology and design sequence, clarification of the gate labels, and the applicant's position on a crossing marshal. We will take a ten-minute break before the questions on drainage.

Cinder Reach Energy Park — Open-floor hearing, continued
21 October 2026, afternoon session

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We are back on the record. The next item is drainage at the temporary construction entrance and its connection with the ordinary watercourse. I will take the applicant's explanation first, then questions. Please say if a drawing number is wrong; there have been several versions today.

Niko Darr: For Vellum Tidal Infrastructure Ltd, the current proposal is a lined settlement basin within construction parcel CP-4. Drawing CR-DR-026, revision C, shows the basin and a temporary overflow to the eastern ditch. The overflow is not proposed as a permanent outfall. I need to correct something I said this morning: the ditch is outside the highway boundary, not inside it. Our drainage witness can provide the ownership note after the hearing.

Elian Sorrell: Is that the same ditch which floods the footpath at the bend? I do not think the drawing shows where the water goes when the basin is full. It puts a blue arrow at the page edge and then, effectively, stops. I asked this in my written representation and got an answer about maintenance rather than capacity.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Mr Sorrell, could you identify the footpath by its recorded number?

Elian Sorrell: Footpath 6, between Fenmere Copse and Reedhook Lane. Sorry, I've got the paper map upside down. The bend is east of the entrance, not west. There are badger setts in Fenmere Copse, which is why I also want to know whether ditch clearance is included in the ecology drawings. I am not asking for a map of the setts to be published.

Niko Darr: The blue arrow is intended to indicate flow into the existing ditch network. It does look as though it ends abruptly in the PDF. We can provide the downstream catchment plan, with any protected-species detail removed from the public copy. Ditch clearance would be limited to the reach shown on drawing CR-DR-026; there is no proposal to clear the whole footpath side.

Iris Pell: Can I come in there? My concern is what happens during the works, not just when the basin has been built. I live at 14 Reedhook Lane, Fenmere, FM4 6QP, and the water already comes across our drive after heavy rain. I am 74 and I can't move the sandbags myself any more. That is not an engineering objection, I know, but somebody needs to be responsible on the first wet morning when the lorries start coming. I have lived in this area for over 40 years. I am not saying every puddle is the applicant's fault.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Thank you. The address can be removed from the published transcript; the point about the construction phase remains. Do you have a question about the proposed monitoring?

Iris Pell: Yes. Who do I ring before six in the morning? The board at the site says enquiries@cinderreach.example, but an email won't stop a driver using the gate while water is running over the road. I don't sleep well when it rains now. My health is affected by the worry, but I am not asking this panel to decide that. I want a named duty role and a number that is answered, even if the person changes.

Niko Darr: There will be a staffed construction contact number, not an individual's mobile on the gate. I cannot give a tested number today. The contractor's incident procedure requires a supervisor to assess standing water at the entrance before deliveries are admitted. I accept that the present wording says 'during normal hours' without explaining a pre-start inspection. We will put forward an amendment to the construction environmental management plan.

Elian Sorrell: That still leaves the ditch. At the site walkover I marked what I thought was a badger sett at the base of the split willow, 3 metres north of culvert C2 beside Footpath 6. Please do not put that marker into a public plan merely to answer my question. The ecology team can check it against their confidential material.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Agreed. The precise location just spoken should be withheld from the public transcript and dealt with in the confidential ecology record. The question for this hearing is whether the proposed drainage works might affect protected features and, if so, what control prevents work proceeding before the check. Mr Darr, please answer that question rather than identifying the feature.

Niko Darr: There is a pre-works ecology hold point for the ditch reach. No clearance can begin until the ecological clerk of works has checked the work area and signed the permit. The public version can describe the control without giving a point location.

Cllr Bracken Firth: My written question 12 was about who can suspend deliveries, not who can write an incident report afterwards. Can the applicant confirm the supervisor actually has that authority? Residents at the bend won't know which subcontractor has turned up on a particular day.

Niko Darr: Yes, the site supervisor can suspend arrivals at either gate. I will make sure the revised plan states that expressly, including how the decision is passed to hauliers. I don't want to imply the parish has to police it.

Iris Pell: There is one more thing, and I may have got this muddled with the earlier access item. My neighbour, Dr Owen Keswick, has a conviction for assault arising from an argument at the lane gate. I mention it because I don't want residents told to sort out traffic disputes among ourselves. It should be the contractor's job. I can send the photograph of the blocked turning area, but it shows a registration number and I'd rather check the image first.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: The personal allegation is not needed to understand the traffic-management point and will not appear in the public record. Please send the photograph to the case team if you wish, with a note identifying what it shows. We can consider whether an edited version is appropriate. We have the request for an answered contact route and an explicit power to pause deliveries. Those are useful, concrete actions.

Niko Darr: Understood. For avoidance of doubt, the applicant will answer those alongside the catchment plan, rather than wait for the next hearing. The corrected public documents will be placed at https://cinderreach.example/documents. I cannot promise the final drawing by Friday, but we will tell the case team on Friday what remains outstanding.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: That concludes drainage for today. We will issue an action list with drawing references checked against the revisions actually before us.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: That concludes drainage for today. We will issue an action list with drawing references checked against the revisions actually before us.

[11.42 am. The hearing moved to construction access and ecology.]

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We are now on item five. I want to keep the discussion to the temporary access from Kiln Lane and the relationship between the haul route and the southern field boundary. Mr Darr, please say which drawing you are using before referring to a gate number. We had three different gate numbers in the drainage session.

Niko Darr: Yes. I am using access drawing CR-AC-09, revision C, for Vellum Tidal Infrastructure Ltd. The construction entrance is marked G7 on that drawing. The proposed wheel wash is inside the site, not on Kiln Lane, and the banksman would stand within the fenced compound.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Thank you. Mr Sorrell, your question was about what happens when a delivery cannot enter straight away.

Elian Sorrell: That's right. The swept-path picture shows one lorry turning in. It doesn't show the next one arriving while somebody's trying to get out. The lay-by on Kiln Lane is used by walkers, and it isn't a holding area just because it looks empty in a computer drawing. Can the applicant put in writing where a vehicle goes if G7 is shut? I also asked this in my representation, IP-CR-01472, but the response just says deliveries will be managed.

Niko Darr: There is no proposal to hold vehicles in that lay-by. The booking system assigns arrival slots. If access is temporarily unavailable, a driver would be instructed before reaching Kiln Lane to remain at the off-site logistics compound. I accept the compound isn't identified in the current construction traffic plan. We can supply its location and the instruction issued to drivers.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please do. An instruction that depends on reaching the driver before the turn needs to say who makes the call and when. Cllr Bracken Firth also asked, in written question WQ-17, whether the council's proposed verge works would overlap the construction period. I don't need an answer invented at the table.

Niko Darr: Understood. We will check that with the highway authority and give a dated answer. I should correct one thing: the booking system isn't yet operating. It is a proposed control, not an existing one.

Iris Pell: Can I come in on the real-life bit? I live at 8 Thimble Row, Merewick MR7 4QJ, and the lane outside our turning is narrow enough that a delivery van waits when a tractor comes the other way. I'm 68, so I won't pretend I can dash across with shopping if there are lorries reversing. I have diagnosed asthma; dust off an unsurfaced waiting area would be a problem for me. The drawings show neat arrows but not the school bus stopping opposite the turning. I'm not saying stop all deliveries. I'm asking who I ring when something's actually blocking the road, and whether that person can stop the next vehicle.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: That is a clear question. Please do not give a private telephone number aloud. The applicant can identify a staffed, shared contact route in its answer, including what authority that contact has to suspend deliveries. Ms Pell, is the bus stop in the position shown on revision C?

Iris Pell: No. It moved last spring, about two lamp posts towards the bend. I can send a photograph, but I don't want the children in it put on the examination website.

Niko Darr: We can check the stop position on site. Our project mailbox, access@cinderreach.example, can receive the photograph if Ms Pell chooses to send it. We would provide a marked-up plan for the public record rather than upload an unedited photograph.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Good. Please route it through the case team so there is a record of what was received. Mr Sorrell, you also raised ecology at G7. Keep to what is necessary for your question; we do not need precise locations of sensitive species read into a public transcript.

Elian Sorrell: I understand. My general point is that badgers have been seen along the southern boundary and bats use the Kiln Lane hedgerow. That's not a reason to abandon an entrance, but it is a reason not to move a fence on a Friday afternoon and call it minor. The applicant's ecologist told us the survey map was updated after the design froze. Which version controls the fencing? I should say that the sett marked S2 is beneath the eastern lip of culvert CR-4, 12 metres north of gate G7. Sorry, I've given the exact place when you asked me not to.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We will consider how that part of the record is published. For the question, Mr Darr, can you answer without repeating the location?

Niko Darr: Yes. The later survey is the one used for the draft ecological management plan. There is still a mismatch between its fence line and revision C of the access drawing. We will submit a reconciled drawing, with a public version that does not disclose the sensitive feature. The ecological clerk of works must approve any fence movement before work, but that requirement ought to be in the plan, not just said here.

Iris Pell: One other thing, and I know this may not be relevant. My neighbour Dr Owen Keswick was convicted in 2022 of taking fuel from the former depot. People keep suggesting I ask that neighbour to monitor the gate, which isn't fair to either of us. I don't want a volunteer arrangement; I want the applicant's contact to take responsibility.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We do not need anyone's history to decide the contact arrangements. The action is for the applicant to specify a staffed route, an escalation procedure and a power to pause deliveries. The case team will review the transcript before publication. Is there anything further on access that cannot be put in the written answer?

Elian Sorrell: No. Please just make sure the revised drawing has a date and revision letter. Last time we were comparing different versions without knowing it.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Agreed. We will break for lunch and resume at 1.15 pm with the construction programme.

Cinder Reach Energy Park — Open floor hearing, construction programme (continued)
21 October 2026, 1.15 pm

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We are back on the record. Before lunch we agreed an action about the delivery contact, not an arrangement involving residents. Mr Darr, please take us through the sequence on slide 12. The screen is a little small, so give us the document revision as well.

Niko Darr: Certainly. This is the Construction Programme, revision C, submitted on 14 October. Vellum Tidal Infrastructure Ltd proposes to build the inland access first, then the cable crossing and finally the generating compound. That order keeps the heaviest loads off Marsh Lane while the temporary turning area is formed. The dates are indicative until the highway authority approves the traffic management plan.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: When does the temporary turning area become usable, as distinct from merely being constructed?

Niko Darr: After surfacing, drainage and a swept-path check. I cannot give a calendar day today. We have said six to eight weeks from the start of that package, although weather could affect it.

Iris Pell: Sorry, but that is the gap I'm worried about. The lorries have to go somewhere during those weeks. The drawing shows a holding point on the other side of the bend. From my front room I cannot see round that bend, and a driver coming up behind a stopped lorry cannot see it either. I have lived here for 40+ years; that isn't a claim to know traffic engineering, just what happens when two vehicles meet there.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Mr Darr, does the programme assume deliveries before the turning area has passed its check?

Niko Darr: Only materials for the access works, not abnormal loads. I accept that the schedule ought to say so expressly. The holding point would be managed by a marshal, not used as overnight parking.

Iris Pell: Last time the marshal disappeared at about four. I felt stressed waiting for school traffic to get through. I am 71, and I can't be expected to stand at the gate ringing people until someone picks up. That is why the staffed number matters. Please don't put my own number into a rota; I gave 07700 936 482 to the case team so they could check a transcript correction, not to contractors.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: That number is not an operational contact. We will make that clear in the action log. The point about the marshal is a proper question for the applicant's revised traffic plan.

Elian Sorrell: Can I ask about the drainage works in the same period? Drawing CR-DR-118, revision B, has the ditch being piped before the access is surfaced. If there is a storm, water currently spreads into the lower field. The new bund seems to send it towards the houses, unless I'm reading the shading backwards.

Niko Darr: You are reading the shading correctly, but the temporary outfall is missing from that simplified slide. It is on drawing CR-DR-119. I can arrange for a combined drawing rather than asking people to flick between them.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please do. And label the temporary and permanent arrangements separately. The ExA needs to understand what happens on a wet day during construction, not simply the final design.

Elian Sorrell: One more point, ecology. I don't want a public drawing that pins down wildlife. The survey says badgers are present in Brindle Wood, which is sufficient for my question. A version circulated at the site walk described the sett entrance as 2.4 metres east of the broken ash stump at the north end of field gate G7. Could that detail be removed from the public combined drawing? What matters for this hearing is whether the trench route can move.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Yes, the case team will check the drawing before it is placed on the public page. Mr Darr, answer the route question without repeating that location.

Niko Darr: There is a micro-siting allowance within the order limits. It does not allow the trench to enter the protected buffer. We will explain the approval step in writing, including who verifies the buffer on site.

Iris Pell: On the programme, could you also say when residents get notice of a change? I asked through planning@vellumtidal.invalid and got an automatic reply saying five working days, but the lane closure leaflet came the evening before. I'm not asking for a guarantee about the weather. I'm asking who tells us when the plan has changed.

Niko Darr: We can specify a minimum notice period for planned closures and a separate procedure for an emergency closure. The project mailbox is the right place to send a query. It will not substitute for notices delivered to affected properties.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Cllr Bracken Firth submitted a written question on exactly that distinction. I will not ask the councillor to repeat it. Ms Pell, your correction form gave your address as 14 Larkspur Fold, Hembrook, HB4 8QN. We do not need to read that into the published action; the applicant can identify affected properties using the agreed notification zone.

Iris Pell: Thank you. My reference is IP-20417 if that helps locate the form. Also, I want to correct something from before lunch. I mentioned Dr Owen Keswick because the suggestion was that my neighbour could watch the gate. That neighbour was convicted of falsifying delivery dockets in 2019, which I should not have brought into a discussion about traffic. It has no bearing on who Vellum employs. I don't want it used as an excuse to leave the gate unstaffed either.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Understood. We will deal with that passage under the normal publication review. No resident is being asked to undertake traffic management. For clarity, the three actions are a phase-by-phase delivery schedule, a combined temporary drainage drawing and a notification procedure with an accountable contact. Mr Darr, can those be provided by 4 November?

Niko Darr: Yes, subject to the highway authority confirming its comments. We will identify any point still provisional rather than implying approval has been given.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Good. We will move to the next agenda item after a short pause.

[Hearing resumed, 11.18 am]

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We are now on Item 5, transport, landscape and water management for the Cinder Reach Energy Park. This is a technical session. I want to start with the assumptions in the revised transport note, not repeat the discussion about notifications. The applicant's note says the construction peak is 86 two-way HGV movements on a weekday. Is that a site-wide maximum or an average across the principal works period?

Niko Darr: A site-wide daily maximum in the current programme. It combines deliveries for the converter compound, cable corridor and temporary works. The average for that period is lower. The note does not propose 86 movements every weekday, and we accept the table heading could make that clearer.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please correct the heading in the version due on 4 November. The highway authority's written response asks for a separate assessment of the junction between Fenbarrow Road and the B4176. Has that been run using the same peak day?

Niko Darr: Yes. Appendix T3 uses that peak, with the quarry traffic already included in the baseline count. There is a small increase in queue length on the Fenbarrow Road arm in the morning model. The junction remains within its modelled capacity, but the result is sensitive to how the existing quarry arrivals are distributed within the hour. We are checking that distribution against the manual count sheets.

Elian Sorrell: Can I check what is meant by a movement? The route drawing shows vehicles leaving by the same gate they enter. I read the table as 86 lorries arriving and 86 leaving, rather than 86 altogether.

Niko Darr: It means 43 arrivals and 43 departures in that example. The drawing gives the route, not an additional set of trips. We should put that explanation beside the table rather than leave it to a footnote.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Agreed. Please also state whether any abnormal loads are included. They appear in a different month on the indicative programme, but the programme may move. What is the management measure if the activities overlap?

Niko Darr: Abnormal loads are excluded from the 86 because they would travel under a separate movement plan. The draft construction traffic management plan prevents those deliveries taking place during the forecast HGV peak. We can make the restriction express, including who must approve a change to the sequence.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Turning to the landscape drawings, Figure LV12 shows the earth bund at its finished height. Figure LV13 shows the opening year, but from a different viewpoint. That makes comparison rather difficult. Can the applicant provide both stages from the same camera position and with the temporary drainage works shown?

Niko Darr: Yes. The temporary swale is in the eastern foreground and was omitted from LV13 because that image was prepared before the drainage revision. The revised image will show the swale, the construction fence and the bund at its initial profile. It will not assume mature planting in year one.

Iris Pell: On that drawing, the green line beside the access track looks like a hedge. Is it a hedge that will be there during construction, or the proposed planting afterwards? It matters to the view across the open ground.

Niko Darr: It is proposed planting afterwards. The key is wrong where it calls that line an existing hedgerow. We will amend the drawing and the landscape schedule. During construction the track edge will have a low safety barrier, not a hedge.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: That correction needs to carry through to the assessment text. An existing hedge and planting that may take several seasons to establish cannot be treated as equivalent screening. Does the assessment rely on that line for its conclusion on the opening-year effect?

Niko Darr: The conclusion remains a moderate adverse effect at the nearest public viewpoint in the opening year. The correction may change the description of what is visible, but we will review the judgment rather than simply state that it is unchanged.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Thank you. Now drainage. The combined drawing requested before the pause should distinguish clean runoff, water from the working areas and the discharge permitted under the surface-water strategy. At present arrows from the temporary haul road seem to stop at the edge of Sheet D4. Where does that flow go during Phase 2?

Niko Darr: It runs to the temporary settlement basin north of the converter compound. The arrows stop because Sheet D4 and Sheet D5 were exported separately. That is a drafting problem, not an unmodelled outfall. The basin has been sized for the Phase 2 contributing area using the design storm stated in Drainage Note DN6.

Elian Sorrell: The phase drawing also shows the basin being removed before the permanent pond is complete. Is there a gap in treatment during that changeover?

Niko Darr: No gap is intended. The permanent pond must be operational before the temporary basin is decommissioned. The bars on the programme overlap, but the key does not explain the dependency. We will add a hold point to the phasing schedule and show the diversion route on the combined drawing.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please make the hold point enforceable in the proposed requirement, not only descriptive in a drawing. I also need confirmation from Mirefen County Council as lead local flood authority on the revised sequence. If its response is not available by 4 November, identify precisely what remains outstanding.

Niko Darr: We will do that. We will submit the modelling inputs with the drawing, so the receiving authority can check the contributing areas rather than infer them from coloured arrows.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Finally, policy compliance. The planning statement refers to Mirefen Local Plan Policy TR7 for access and Policy EN4 for landscape character. It should explain how the temporary construction effects have been considered as well as the finished development. I am not inviting a new statement of general support for the project; I am asking for a traceable account of the effects, proposed controls and residual judgments.

Niko Darr: Understood. We will provide a short policy table cross-referencing the revised transport note, the corrected visualisations and the combined drainage drawing. Where a document is still awaiting consultation comments, the table will say so.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Those are the actions for Item 5. The examination timetable is unchanged. We will take the next item after lunch.

AFTERNOON SESSION — ITEM 6: CONSTRUCTION ACCESS AND RESIDENT NOTIFICATION

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Good afternoon. The recording has restarted. We are dealing with construction access, drainage works where those works affect the highway, and how residents will be told about changes. This is not a reopening of the policy discussion before lunch. Could the applicant first identify what has changed in the access plan since the last hearing?

Niko Darr: On behalf of Vellum Tidal Infrastructure Ltd, the revised plan retains the eastern haul route but moves the temporary wheel-wash bay away from the ditch. The change is shown on drawing CR-AC-021, revision C. The applicant has also proposed a daily check of the outfall during the culvert works. That check is in the draft construction environmental management plan, although the location of the check point is not yet marked on the drawing.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Thank you. Elian Sorrell, you asked to come back on the position of the temporary gate.

Elian Sorrell: Yes. The coloured line on the new drawing goes through the gate, but the text says the gate is for emergency use only. I cannot tell whether delivery vehicles will turn there when the main route floods. The ditch has come over the road twice this year. I would like a straight answer, not another note saying the arrangements will be agreed later. Cllr Bracken Firth asked much the same question in the written questions.

Niko Darr: The applicant does not propose routine use of that gate. If the eastern route becomes unavailable, deliveries would stop pending an agreed alternative. I accept that the word 'emergency' is doing too much work in the current note. We can make clear that it covers access for emergency services and not an unapproved diversion for HGVs.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please do. I also want the relevant paragraph of the traffic management plan corrected, rather than an explanation existing only in the transcript. Iris Pell, you indicated you wished to speak about notification.

Iris Pell: I do. I am 67 and I have lived beside Marshglass Lane for over 40 years. I am not asking the applicant to stop every lorry. I am asking to know when the road will be narrowed and when the culvert is being opened up. Last time, a notice was put on a gate at the far end, where people going towards the village wouldn't see it. My health is affected by the uncertainty and the poor sleep, but the practical point is that I need enough warning to arrange a different way out.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Is your concern about a particular closure or about the method of giving notice generally?

Iris Pell: Both. The letter says 'local properties' without saying which ones. My home is 18 Sedgeglass Row, Fenmere, FM4 8QT, and that is on the route where the banksman is proposed. I appreciate the address may be taken out of the published transcript. I also tried sending the query to info@vellumtidal.example, which is printed on the leaflet, and got a standard reply about the exhibition. It didn't answer whether residents would be able to leave by car during the pour.

Niko Darr: The current proposal is to maintain escorted access during the pour, except for two short lifting operations. The exact times cannot responsibly be fixed before the contractor's method statement is approved. What can be fixed is a minimum period for advance notice and a person able to answer an access question on the day. The generic mailbox should route that sort of question to the construction team, and evidently the leaflet needs to say more.

Iris Pell: There is another reason I don't want messages sent round through neighbours. Dr Owen Keswick, who lives next door and is not involved in this examination, was convicted of falsifying vehicle inspection certificates in 2019. I don't think it is fair to ask that household to collect everyone's vehicle details or pass on requests for escorted access. Please deal with residents directly.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: I will interrupt there. We do not need any account of a neighbour's history to determine the notification arrangements, and that material should not be repeated. The point about direct notification is understood. Please keep questions addressed to the applicant's proposal rather than to other residents.

Elian Sorrell: On that proposal, will the direct notice cover a sudden change caused by water levels? Mirefen County Council's response says the temporary drainage connection must be inspected before the culvert is opened. The programme drawing seems to put the opening first. That is why access and drainage cannot be split into separate answers.

Niko Darr: That sequence is an error in the programme drawing. The connection is to be inspected first. The combined drainage drawing mentioned this morning will show the inspection hold point and the corresponding traffic restriction. If water levels require a change on the day, the applicant proposes a telephone and door-to-door notification process for affected properties, as well as an update on the project website.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please submit the proposed wording for that process, including who decides that a change has occurred and how an unanswered door will be dealt with. Do not provide a list of residents' names or telephone numbers in the examination document.

Elian Sorrell: One last ecology point. The survey summary says only that badger activity occurs in Brackenwash Wood. I agree that a broad description is sufficient for the public summary. During the site walk I was shown a sett at the north end of culvert C4, 12 metres east of gate G2. If the inspection point moves, the applicant needs to check the working area against the confidential survey plan, not put the precise position in a public drawing.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Agreed. The public drawing should show the working-area limit and the control required, without identifying a protected site. I have recorded four actions: the gate wording, the corrected drainage and traffic sequence, the resident notification procedure, and the check against the confidential ecology material. The applicant should cross-reference the revised documents in the policy table requested under Item 5. We will now move to questions on noise.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We will now move to questions on noise. For clarity, this item concerns the construction assessment and the operational plant assumptions. The revised traffic and drainage sequence will be dealt with in the action already recorded; I do not want the same timetable expressed differently in three documents.

Niko Darr: Understood. For Vellum Tidal Infrastructure Ltd, the construction noise assessment uses the programme in Appendix 6B, revision C. It assumes piling at the western compound for six weeks, followed by foundations at the converter building. Those are sequential activities in the model. The table in the environmental statement made them look concurrent because both were placed under the same quarter. We will correct the table, not change the model.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Does that correction alter the predicted maximum at the nearest assessment location?

Niko Darr: No. The maximum remains during foundation works, when the mobile crane and concrete pumps operate together. The model includes the temporary acoustic screen shown on drawing CR-AN-04. Without that screen the prediction would exceed the daytime criterion used in the assessment, so its installation is a committed mitigation measure rather than an option for the contractor.

Elian Sorrell: Can the drawing say when it goes up? At present it says ‘as required’, while the assessment assumes it is there before the pumps start. Also, the route for delivering the screen panels appears to cross the drainage working area at culvert C4.

Niko Darr: That is a fair drafting point. The panels can enter from the western compound access. We will replace ‘as required’ with a hold point: the screen must be installed and checked before the foundation plant is brought into use. We will add the delivery route to the construction logistics plan so it is consistent with the culvert sequence.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Turning to operation, the night-time calculation uses the manufacturer’s guaranteed sound-power level for the cooling units. Is there any allowance for tonal character?

Niko Darr: Yes. A tonal correction is included in the rating level in Table 8.12, though the table heading currently describes the uncorrected specific level. That heading needs changing. The proposed requirement would cap the rating level at the monitoring locations shown on drawing CR-AN-07; compliance would be checked after commissioning with all normal cooling units available for duty.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Please show the calculation chain in one place, including the correction, the operating scenario and the applicable limit. Do not rely on a reader finding those separately in the appendices. The action is a corrected noise table, a firm screen-installation hold point and a consolidated operational compliance schedule. We will take a short break before the questions on landscape effects.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: We resume with landscape effects. Mr Darr, is the planting on drawing CR-LV-12 a commitment or an illustration?

Niko Darr: It is intended as a commitment for Vellum Tidal Infrastructure Ltd. The species mix may change following soil testing, but the boundary width will not.

Elian Sorrell: Who checks that width? The plan shows a gap beside the eastern access track, exactly where the view from the footpath opens up.

Niko Darr: We can provide a dimensioned revision at the next deadline.

Iris Pell: I am 68, and I use that footpath most mornings. Construction traffic already worries me. My neighbour, Dr Owen Keswick, was convicted of fly-tipping in 2019, so please don't treat his account of what is on that verge as mine. I am asking about the screening, not him.

Inspector Tamsin Vale: Understood. We will not address that personal matter. Cllr Bracken Firth also asked when the planting would be established. Please answer that in the revision.

text:
Written representation: Brindle Mere Solar Farm
Application reference: BM/NSIP/2026/04
From: Rowan Fenn
Interested Party reference: IP-462917
Address for correspondence: 14 Willow Lantern Lane, Larchwick, LB4 7QP
Email: rowan.fenn@meadowmail.example

I object to the proposed Brindle Mere Solar Farm. My house faces the fields beside Lantern Lane and I use the lane on foot most days. I am not against solar power. I am against putting a development of this size here without properly showing what it would mean for the people, farmland and wildlife already in this small valley. The drawings make the site look like a neat rectangle. On the ground it is a series of sloping fields, with hedges, wet corners and narrow roads between homes.

The landscape assessment relies too much on views from the main road. From our side of Larchwick the panels would be seen against the rising ground, not screened by it. The proposed planting might help eventually, but a line of small trees will not hide fencing, cameras and inverter buildings for years. Please do not treat a photomontage showing mature planting as if it describes what residents will see when the scheme opens. I have lived in this area for over 40 years, and the open view across the valley is one reason people walk this route.

I am particularly concerned about construction traffic. Lantern Lane has no pavement after the bend by Ash Sedge Farm, and two vehicles already struggle to pass there. The transport assessment counts vehicles but does not describe what happens when a delivery meets someone walking with a pushchair or a person on a mobility scooter. Our neighbour, Tessa Bramley, regularly walks that bend to reach the bus stop and is not making a representation herself. There should be a properly measured passing plan, with drawings showing the actual widths between the hedgebanks, before any construction route is approved. A promise that drivers will be briefed is not enough.

My 11-year-old son has diagnosed asthma. I understand that ordinary construction dust is not the same thing as a permanent air-quality problem, but I want enforceable controls rather than a sentence saying water bowsers may be used if needed. At present the draft construction plan leaves the person deciding whether dust is excessive as the contractor doing the work. Dust monitoring should be specified at the nearest homes, with a clear trigger for stopping earthworks in dry, windy weather. This is not a request to stop the project because of one household; it is a request to make the controls real.

The ecology material also needs checking on the ground. Badger setts have been identified in Sallowbank Wood, which is a broad area and not a reason to publish their precise positions. However, I have given the case team a separate confidential note because one sett is in the spoil hollow 18 metres east of the northern gate to field 6, immediately beneath the lone hawthorn marked H7 on access plan AS-03. Please keep that detail out of any public plan. I am not claiming to be an ecologist. My point is that the access track and compound boundary seem to have moved between drawings, while the survey conclusions have not been updated to match. There are also bats feeding along the western hedge in summer; that observation does not tell me where any roost is.

The applicant says the land can return to agriculture after the operating period. That sounds reassuring, but the soil handling drawings do not show how the wetter parts will avoid compaction when cable trenches are opened. The field by the lower drain holds water after ordinary rain. If the ground is stripped and tracked over at the wrong time, a promise to restore it later will be difficult to test. I would like the Examining Authority to require a soil plan with field-by-field limits and independent records, not just a general commitment to good practice. The proposed drainage swales should also be checked against the places where water already crosses Lantern Lane.

I have a separate concern about the provenance of the panels. I believe Merecombe Solar Developments Limited has used forced labour in the supply chain for Brindle Mere Solar Farm. The examination should require transparent evidence about manufacturing and procurement rather than accepting a broad assurance that suppliers follow a code. Xinjiang is regularly mentioned in public discussions about solar supply chains, but a reference to a place is not, by itself, proof about any particular shipment. The war in Ukraine is another reason to think seriously about secure energy supplies. Neither issue excuses an inadequate explanation of where the equipment for this particular project will come from.

Cllr Elian Voss said at the open meeting that residents should put specific questions into the examination, so mine are these: which drawing governs the final access route; who can order dusty work to stop; and when will the updated habitat and soil information be available for comment? I sent similar questions to info@larchwickparish.example and have not had a substantive reply. I know consultation takes time, but being told to look at a large bundle of revised documents is not the same as being shown what changed. The process has left me worried and sleeping poorly. I do not ask for those feelings to be treated as technical evidence; I ask for the underlying questions to be answered.

Please recommend refusal unless the applicant demonstrates a workable access arrangement, reliable environmental controls and a clear procurement audit. If consent is granted, those matters should be requirements that can be enforced, not aspirations left for later agreement. Please also ensure residents can comment on any revised construction route before it is fixed.

Rowan Fenn

Supplementary objection: Brindle Mere Solar Farm
18 October 2026
From: Rowan Fenn

I am adding this note because the applicant's latest response does not resolve the points in my earlier objection. I have lived in Larchwick for 40+ years. That does not make me an expert, but it does mean I know how quickly the lane floods when the ditch beside Footpath 4 is blocked. The construction traffic assessment seems to assume that the lane and its verges will be available in the same condition throughout the build. They are not in that condition now. The applicant should identify who will inspect the ditch, who will clear it, and how residents will report a problem without being passed between contractors.

The revised access drawing shows a passing place near the bend, but it does not say what happens when a delivery arrives while the school bus is stopped. A swept-path diagram is not a timetable. Please ask for the expected delivery hours, the maximum number of movements on the busiest day and a plan for vehicles that arrive early. I would also like the applicant to explain whether its proposed banksman can actually see both approaches from the position marked on the plan. These are practical questions, not a request for a perfect road.

Mrs Tessa Bramley told me she sometimes has to reverse towards that bend when two large vehicles meet. She lives next to me and is not making a representation of her own. I mention the conversation to explain why the passing-place detail matters, not as evidence of the traffic figures. At the open meeting, Cllr Elian Voss asked whether the route could be changed after consent. I understood the answer to be that the final traffic plan would come later. If that is correct, residents need a proper opportunity to see and comment on it before it is approved.

My home is at 7 Willow Fold, Larchwick, Fenmere FM4 8QT, and the bedrooms face the proposed temporary compound. My daughter, Anwen Fenn, aged 14, has diagnosed asthma. I am not suggesting that every dusty day will make her ill. I am asking what measurable trigger will stop earthworks when dust crosses the site boundary, rather than leaving a contractor to decide whether it looks acceptable. The proposed complaints log would be more useful if it recorded the time of the report, wind direction, action taken and time of reply. Poor sleep and worry are already affecting our household, but those feelings are separate from the question of whether the dust controls will work.

On ecology, the survey summary says badgers use the wider area. Last spring I saw fresh digging in the hedge at the north-west corner of field P17, 6 metres east of the stile on Larchwick Footpath 4. I have not published a photograph because I do not want people going to look for it. I ask the Examining Authority to have the ecology team check this confidentially before any clearance is permitted. Bats were recorded in Holloway Wood, but that broad statement does not show whether the proposed lighting at the compound has been assessed against the routes they use. The fencing drawings should also say how small animals will pass through or around the perimeter. These matters can be dealt with, but they cannot simply be left to a general promise to protect wildlife.

I allege that Merecombe Solar Developments Limited has knowingly benefited from forced labour in its solar-panel supply chain for the Brindle Mere Solar Farm project. This is a serious allegation, and I recognise that I have not seen the applicant's purchase contracts. The concern is that an assurance from the immediate supplier does not tell us where the silicon and other components originated. Reports about Xinjiang have made many people ask for traceability, and the war in Ukraine has shown how quickly supply arrangements can change. Neither point proves where these particular panels will come from. That is why I want an independent procurement audit, with a method for checking changes of supplier, before equipment is ordered. I do not think a statement that suppliers must obey the law is enough on its own.

The applicant's statement about local benefit also needs to be more precise. A community fund is welcome in principle, but the amount described in the consultation leaflet is not a substitute for controlling construction impacts. Nor should the prospect of cheaper electricity be presented as a guaranteed saving to each household. I would rather see a clear account of who administers the fund, when it begins and whether payments continue if the scheme changes hands. These are questions about the proposal, not objections to renewable energy as such.

For completeness, my earlier email came from rowan.fenn@homepost.example. The reference on the acknowledgement was IP-684209. I can provide the photograph of the lane verge privately if it assists, but please do not put my address or the ecology detail on a public map. I have also seen a traffic photograph circulated at https://marsh-watch.example/records/2026; I cannot verify when it was taken, so it should not be used instead of a current site visit. General information about the examination is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/planning-inspectorate, but finding the correct revised drawing in the examination library remains difficult for residents.

I ask the Examining Authority to recommend refusal if the applicant cannot settle these matters during the examination. If it can, the access plan, dust thresholds, ecological checks and procurement audit should be secured by requirements with named responsibilities and points at which work must stop. Please do not approve wording that merely says details will be agreed later without stating what those details must achieve.

Rowan Fenn

Further comments on Brindle Mere Solar Farm

I am sending this as a further note because the applicant's latest response appears to answer a different question from the one residents actually raised. I do not object to renewable energy in principle. I object to this layout, the uncertainty about how it will be built, and the suggestion that the outstanding matters can all be dealt with after consent. For reference, my Interested Party number is IP-452816. I have lived in Larchwick for over 40 years, and I use the lanes and footpaths around the site most weeks.

The construction traffic table gives an average number of deliveries. An average is not much help if several long vehicles arrive together at the school-run time or when farm vehicles are using Mere Lane. The swept-path drawing shows a clean road and an unobstructed junction. In practice there are parked cars, a ditch edge which has broken away in places, and people on foot because there is no continuous pavement. My neighbour, Tessa Bramley, has described seeing two vans mount the verge at the bend last month. Tessa is not taking part in the examination, and I am not putting forward that account as a formal traffic survey. It is a reason to check the drawing on the ground rather than treating it as proof that the route works.

At the open meeting Cllr Elian Voss asked who would record complaints about blocked access and how quickly the contractor would have to respond. I could not find a clear answer in the applicant's subsequent note. A number to ring is useful only if someone has authority to tell a driver to turn around or stop a delivery. Please require a delivery booking system, a named role responsible for the route, and a public record of incidents. The generic parish address, planning@larchwick-parish.example, could receive copies, but it should not be left to Larchwick Parish to manage the contractor.

I also want to correct the impression that the only people affected by dust will be those immediately beside the panels. My home is at 7 Thistledown Close, Larchwick, LW8 4QN, and wind from the bare fields reaches our back garden. My daughter Anwen Fenn, aged 14, has been diagnosed with asthma. I understand that a construction dust plan cannot promise no dust at all, but a trigger level, a way of measuring it and an enforceable pause in earthworks would make a real difference. Simply saying that water bowsers will be available does not explain when they will be used. I have had poor sleep worrying about this; that is not a medical assessment of the scheme, just why I am pressing for a condition that can actually be checked.

The ecology response also needs more care. Badger signs in Brindle Copse have been discussed in public, which is a broad description, not a survey record. In a note I made while walking the permissive path, I recorded that the sett entrance is beside the second willow, 18 metres east of the stile on Footpath LW/7, at grid reference NX 31472 60839. That detail should not be put on an unrestricted public plan. My point is that a qualified ecologist should inspect the affected works area immediately before clearance and that the method of protecting any active sett should be settled before machinery arrives. I am not asking the Examining Authority to rely on my identification instead of a proper survey.

On procurement, I believe Merecombe Solar Developments Limited is using forced labour in the supply chain for Brindle Mere Solar Farm. The applicant has not, in my view, provided the traceability needed to answer that concern. Xinjiang is mentioned frequently in discussions about solar components, but a place name alone proves nothing about a particular shipment. What I want is an independently checked account of where the panels and their principal components will come from, what documents will be inspected, and what happens if the supplier cannot produce them. A promise to follow a policy is not the same as a test of the actual order placed for this project. Any audit should take place before procurement is locked in, not after the equipment is on site.

The war in Ukraine is another reason people talk about energy security, and I accept that the country needs to move away from fossil fuels. It does not follow that every proposed solar layout is suitable, or that supply-chain scrutiny can be skipped for speed. These are separate questions. I would welcome a design that keeps the better-used path open, provides reliable screening without planting over drainage features, and makes its procurement commitments capable of enforcement. The applicant's revised drawing appears to move the fence in one location but leaves the explanation of maintenance access unclear.

For completeness, a link circulated in the village discussion was https://fields-and-futures.example/posts/brindle-lorry-video. I have no way of confirming the date or location of that clip and do not ask you to treat it as evidence. The examination documents on https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/planning-inspectorate are the material I have tried to use, although the numbering of replacement plans has been confusing. My earlier reference to the verge was about the southern bend, not the entrance to the substation. I hope that correction prevents my comment being attached to the wrong drawing.

If a hearing is arranged, please let me know through the examination's usual correspondence route. My email is rowan.fenn@post.example and my telephone number is 07700 900 472, but I would prefer the substance of any answer to appear in the public examination record. I am not asking for a private assurance. The applicant should show, in a document everyone can see, how traffic will be stopped when the lane is unsafe, how dust and ecology checks will work, and how the procurement audit will be verified. Without those safeguards I maintain my objection.

Rowan Fenn

Further comments on construction traffic, drainage and landscape effects

The corrected access drawing still does not demonstrate that construction traffic can safely use the southern bend of Fenfold Lane. The swept-path plot shows a delivery vehicle passing a car, but assumes a clear carriageway and does not account for the narrowing caused by the drainage grips. The Construction Traffic Management Plan should identify the maximum vehicle dimensions, the number of deliveries in each construction phase and the circumstances in which a banksman or temporary closure would be required. A statement that deliveries will be scheduled outside peak periods is not enough: the plan needs an enforceable daily limit and a method for recording departures as well as arrivals.

The traffic assessment also treats the junction with Mere Road as having adequate visibility without showing the seasonal height of the boundary vegetation. If cutting is proposed, the drawings should distinguish vegetation within the highway from land requiring a separate agreement. Merecombe County Council should be asked to confirm which visibility standard it has assessed. This matters particularly for the transformer delivery, which appears in the programme as a single movement but is not included in the representative swept-path drawings. These are matters capable of being resolved with revised drawings, rather than promises left to a contractor after consent.

On drainage, the proposed swales are shown outside the panel areas, yet several temporary compounds occupy the same low ground during construction. The phasing plan should explain where runoff goes before the permanent swales are operational, and how exposed soil will be kept out of Brindle Mere after heavy rain. The Flood Risk and Drainage Addendum refers to inspections ‘as necessary’ but gives neither a trigger rainfall depth nor a schedule for clearing sediment traps. A drawing that places a trap on a plan does not establish that it will function throughout the earthworks period.

Merecombe Solar Developments Limited also relies heavily on hedge growth to reduce views of Brindle Mere Solar Farm. The Year 1 and Year 15 visualisations should use the same viewpoint and camera height; at present the comparison is difficult because the crop and foreground differ. The proposed hedge along the eastern edge is interrupted at two maintenance gates, leaving a direct view towards the inverter cabins. This gap should be assessed as part of the operational landscape effect, not treated as a construction-only feature. Badger activity in Brindle Copse is mentioned in the ecology material, but no specific location is needed in the public traffic or landscape drawings. Overall, the mitigation should be fixed to identifiable plans and phases so that its effectiveness can be tested during the examination.

The construction traffic assessment also needs a consistent worst-case scenario. Merecombe Solar Developments Limited gives an average of 18 HGV movements per day, but the delivery programme for Brindle Mere Solar Farm shows panels, mounting frames and stone arriving during the same six-week period. The assessment should model the peak day, not only the average, and include the temporary signal arrangement at the Larchwick Lane–Fenbarrow Road junction. Merecombe County Council should be asked to confirm whether the swept-path drawings allow two agricultural vehicles to pass without mounting the verge.

Drainage is similarly dependent on details deferred until after consent. Drawing BRM-DR-07 shows the proposed swales but not their outfalls or the sequence in which they would become operational. If compound hardstanding is laid before the swales are connected, runoff could reach the roadside ditch untreated. A phasing condition should require the relevant drainage measures to be working before each construction area is opened. These are design matters, not objections to solar generation in principle.
